boundary_rationale: The book's opening words themselves begin the unit: the rare title-superscription דִּבְרֵ֥י נְחֶמְיָ֖ה בֶּן חֲכַלְיָ֑ה ("divrei Nechemyah ben-Chakalyah") — WEB “The words of Nehemiah the son of Hacaliah” — has no antecedent text to compete with for the left edge, fixing 1:1 as the opening verse of the book and of this unit (the OSHB extract carries a ketiv/qere pair on the month name here, כסלו כִּסְלֵיו֙, orthographic and boundary-neutral). The unit carries the Susa setting notice (1:1b) into Hanani's report of the survivors' affliction and Jerusalem's broken wall and burned gates (1:2-3), then closes at 1:4's hearing-response frame וַיְהִ֞י כְּשָׁמְעִ֣י אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה ("vayehi k'shom'i et-hadevarim ha'eleh") — WEB “When I heard these words, I sat down and wept” — the device matrix's own vayehi-kishmoa notice, recurring once more in the book at 13:3 in the same construction (vayehi plus ke-shom'am, ‘when they heard’). The right edge falls at 1:4's own close: the 1cs wayyiqtol chain that closes 1:4 continues directly into 1:5's own va'omar, and the divine title closing 1:4 (Elohei hashamayim) is resumed at once in 1:5's vocative, so nothing in the Hebrew itself breaks at this seam. What marks the edge instead is 1:4's own discourse mode: its closing participle u-mitpallel (“praying”) names the prayer in summary rather than quoting it, while 1:5 opens the quoted content of that same prayer in full — a summary-notice-to-direct-address shift, not a discontinuity, so this row retains 1:4 as its own close and treats the quoted prayer as its own unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival is Neh.1.4-Neh.1.11, the prayer traveling forward with the hinge verse that announces it — 1:4's own participle (u-mitpallel) names the very prayer 1:5-11 supplies, and nothing in the Hebrew itself marks 1:4 as belonging to what precedes rather than what follows. It is not adopted because 1:4 itself completes the hearing-report scene in summary (heard, sat, wept, mourned, fasted, and prayed, all narrated in brief) before any of that content is quoted, while 1:5-11 supplies the prayer's own words in full; the summary notice and its quoted content are kept as separate units on that ground, not on a discontinuity the Hebrew does not show.

boundary_rationale: A tier-1 inclusio brackets this unit: the particle anna opens the prayer at וָאֹמַ֗ר אָֽנָּ֤א יְהוָה֙ (1:5, WEB “I beg you, Yahweh, the God of heaven”) and stands verse-initial again at the prayer's own closing verse, אָנָּ֣א אֲדֹנָ֗י (1:11, WEB “Lord, I beg you, let your ear be attentive now to the prayer of your servant”) — the device matrix's prayer-bracket anna, tier-1 for these edges, sweep: 2 book-wide. The left edge is argued from narrated first-person action giving way to quoted first-person direct address: 1:4 closes on Nehemiah's own narrated weeping and fasting, and 1:5 opens the address itself; confession (1:6-7) and the Mosaic recall (1:8-9, וְשַׁבְתֶּ֣ם אֵלַ֔י, WEB “you return to me”; the same verse carries a second ketiv/qere pair later on, והבואתים וַהֲבִֽיאוֹתִים֙, morphological and non-boundary-bearing) fill the body. The right edge falls at the end of 1:11 inclusive of the cupbearer notice sharing its verse: after the closing petition's own content concludes, the register shifts a second time — to the flat notice וַאֲנִ֛י הָיִ֥יתִי מַשְׁקֶ֖ה לַמֶּֽלֶךְ (WEB “Now I was cup bearer to the king.”) — a role-notice inside the same verse that pivots the narrative toward the fresh occasion opened by 2:1's date frame, rather than opening a new speech unit itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the cupbearer notice (1:11b) forward into the court scene is tempting since it introduces Nehemiah's office, but it sits inside the same verse as the second anna and cannot be pulled loose without splitting mid-verse.

boundary_rationale: A fresh month notice opens the scene, וַיְהִ֣י בְּחֹ֣דֶשׁ נִיסָ֗ן (2:1, WEB “In the month Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king”), the vayehi-be-chodesh frame (sweep: 2 book-wide, matching 1:1's own construction) returning the narrative to court-occasion time and a fresh set of participants rather than the prayer's address register; because both dates carry the identical regnal year-number, the calendar interval between Chislev and Nisan turns on an unstated year-reckoning convention, so the opening edge rests on the frame and the change of occasion and participants alone, not on any settled interval. Inside the audience, the flash-prayer וָֽאֶתְפַּלֵּ֔ל אֶל אֱלֹהֵ֖י הַשָּׁמָֽיִם (2:4, WEB “So I prayed to the God of heaven.”) marks the device matrix's va'etpallel entry, embedded in dialogue rather than framed as its own unit (inset rule). The commission (letters, timber grant) and the escorted journey to the governors beyond the River follow, and the scene closes at 2:10's וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע סַנְבַלַּ֣ט הַחֹרֹנִ֗י (WEB “When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite servant heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly”), the earlier of a matched pair of antagonist-hearing notices repeated near-verbatim at 2:19 (vayyishma Sanballat hachoroni ve-Toviyah ha'eved ha-Ammoni, flanked by tier-3 single-witness PE marks at 2:9 and 2:18), before Nehemiah's own fresh arrival-in-Jerusalem notice at 2:11 — a tier-1 location/occasion restart — opens the next scene. Since a mark is cited, symmetry is disclosed for this unit's own span too: oshb:Neh.1.11 (petuchah, single-witness) precedes it as the front seam, oshb:Neh.2.9 (petuchah, single-witness) falls inside it, and oshb:Neh.2.3 (samekh, single-witness) likewise falls inside it; all tier-3 weak corroboration, none driving the call.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival is 2:1-20 as one unit bracketed by the matched antagonist-hearing notices at 2:10 and 2:19 (vayyishma Sanballat hachoroni ve-Toviyah ha'eved ha-Ammoni, near-verbatim at both, PE marks at 2:9/2:18 tier-3 single-witness); it is defeated by 2:11's fresh arrival-in-Jerusalem notice, a genuine tier-1 location/occasion restart the merged reading would have to overcome and does not.

boundary_rationale: Physical arrival marks the opening, וָאָב֖וֹא אֶל יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם (2:11, WEB “So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days.”), a new occasion distinct from the Susa court scene. The covert night ride follows, framed by the God-into-my-heart motive מָ֗ה אֱלֹהַי֙ נֹתֵ֣ן אֶל לִבִּ֔י (2:12, WEB “what my God put into my heart”), the earlier of the device matrix's two occurrences of this motif (the other at 7:5, different syntax), and circuits the broken gates by night (2:13; the OSHB extract carries a ketiv/qere pair there, המפרוצים הֵ֣ם פְּרוּצִ֔ים, orthographic/word-division and boundary-neutral). The disclosure speech to the officials, לְכ֗וּ וְנִבְנֶה֙ אֶת חוֹמַ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם (2:17, WEB “Come, let's build up the wall of Jerusalem”), and their hand-strengthening response carry the unit toward its close at 2:19-20's second antagonist-hearing notice and Nehemiah's rebuttal, וָאָשִׁ֨יב אוֹתָ֜ם דָּבָ֗ר (2:20, WEB “Then I answered them, and said to them”). That rebuttal closes the commissioning arc in Nehemiah's own narrating voice before an entirely different genre opens at 3:1 with the register's own formula, וַיָּ֡קָם אֶלְיָשִׁיב֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַגָּד֜וֹל וְאֶחָ֣יו הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים וַיִּבְנוּ֙ אֶת שַׁ֣עַר הַצֹּ֔אן (WEB “Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brothers the priests, and they built the sheep gate.”).
strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival is the merged 2:1-20 reading — the matched vayyishma-Sanballat-hachoroni-ve-Toviyah notices bracketing 2:10 and 2:19, as argued at the 2:1-2:10 audience scene — answered by this row's own two tier-1 signals: the fresh arrival-in-Jerusalem notice opening 2:11, and the person shift at the 2:20|3:1 seam from 2:20's 1cs rebuttal (va'ashiv) to 3:1's third-person-plural register subjects, neither of which the merged reading can absorb.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens at a tier-1 discontinuity from the surrounding memoir narration -- the shift from 2:20's 1cs rebuttal verbs to 3:1's third-person-plural register subjects, וַיָּ֡קָם אֶלְיָשִׁיב֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַגָּד֜וֹל וְאֶחָ֣יו הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים וַיִּבְנוּ֙ אֶת שַׁ֣עַר הַצֹּ֔אן (3:1, WEB “Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brothers the priests, and they built the sheep gate.”). 3:1's own וַיָּ֡קָם ("arose") is the register's only occurrence of vayyaqam (sweep: 2 book-wide, Neh.3.1 and Neh.9.4, the latter itself a narrative notice rather than a register entry), and the verse does not carry the register's own accusative-fronted et-sha'ar-plus-door-notice formula that its true station heads share (3:3, 3:6, 3:13, 3:14, 3:15) -- it fronts the verb, with the gate in ordinary post-verbal position, ordinary narration's own clause shape. The high priest's party consecrates it to the towers of Hammeah and Hananel, then the chain-connective proper begins at וְעַל יָד֥וֹ בָנ֖וּ (3:2, WEB “Next to him the men of Jericho built.”), repeated for Zaccur. This opening entry already carries the register's characteristic marking: oshb:Neh.3.1 (samekh, single-witness) and oshb:Neh.3.2 (samekh, single-witness) — the latter a double mark. Such marking recurs at most entries through this part's wall-register span (27 of 32 verses carry at least one mark, 34 marks total, with doubles at 3.2, 3.8, 3.23, and 3.29-3.30 and a triple at 3.4, five verses unmarked), all WLC single-witness; the composition is 33 samekh and a single petuchah closing the register at its terminal verse, cited below; per Writings-corpus policy it is tier-3 weak corroboration at most, drives none of this part's station-seam calls, and its absence at the unmarked entries counts against none of them either. The unit closes before the fish gate opens the register's own accusative-fronted formula at 3:3. The register's terminal petuchah stands at oshb:Neh.3.32 (petuchah, single-witness).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 3:1-2 into a longer opening span through 3:5 is possible since both belong to the same connective chain, but 3:3's named-gate restart is as clean a station boundary as 3:1's, so the finer cut is the more defensible reading.

boundary_rationale: A second named station opens the unit, וְאֵת֙ שַׁ֣עַר הַדָּגִ֔ים בָּנ֖וּ (3:3, WEB “The sons of Hassenaah built the fish gate.”), with its own fuller beams-doors-bolts-bars formula (going beyond 3:1's sheep-gate entry, which sets up just its doors). The register's own predicate switches inside this span, from banah at 3:1-3:3 (vayyivnu/banu/banu) to hecheziq beginning at 3:4 and running through 3:32 (sweep: 26 book-wide); but the register's own gate-station convention outranks this lexical seam: no gate name interrupts across the banah/hecheziq switch, so it marks no boundary of its own. Meremoth, Meshullam, and Zadok continue the al-yadam chain (3:4, a triple-marked verse, WLC single-witness — this part's fuller register-wide mark density is disclosed in the sheep-gate row), and the unit closes on a dissonant note at 3:5, וְאַדִּֽירֵיהֶם֙ לֹא הֵבִ֣יאוּ צַוָּרָ֔ם בַּעֲבֹדַ֖ת אֲדֹנֵיהֶֽם (WEB “but their nobles didn't put their necks to the Lord's work.”) — a named-group entry that breaks the chain's normal compliance pattern and stands as its own closing beat before the old gate opens a fresh station at 3:6.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two rivals compete here: reading 3:5's noncompliant Tekoites as belonging with the old-gate stretch that follows instead, rejected because 3:5 has no gate-name restart of its own and grammatically continues 3:3-4's fish-gate entry, not the old gate's; and the predicate switch itself inviting a 3:1-3:3 banah-block cut against 3:4 onward, rejected because the register's own convention anchors segmentation on named gate-station heads rather than bare predicate alternation, and no gate name marks a restart at 3:4.

boundary_rationale: The old gate opens the station, וְאֵת֩ שַׁ֨עַר הַיְשָׁנָ֜ה הֶחֱזִ֗יקוּ (3:6, WEB “Joiada the son of Paseah and Meshullam the son of Besodeiah repaired the old gate.”), matching 3:3's beams-doors-bolts-bars notice in full (3:1's sheep-gate entry, by contrast, sets up its doors alone, with no beams, bolts, or bars named). The register's connective inventory across this span is al-yadam (3:7, 3:9, 3:10) and al-yado (3:8 twice, including a waw-less עַל יָד֣וֹ heading the first clause of 3:8, then 3:10, 3:12) -- not acharav, which sweeps to 14 occurrences book-wide but does not begin until 3:16, outside this span -- continuing through Melatiah, Uzziel, Hananiah (the wide-wall notice, 3:8), Rephaiah, Jedaiah, Hattush, and the second-portion entry for Malchijah and Hasshub (3:11), asyndetic among the span's ordinary entries (1 of 6 in 3:7-3:12 carrying no al-yadam/al-yado connective: מִדָּ֣ה שֵׁנִ֗ית הֶחֱזִיק֙; 3:6 itself, the station head, opens with the register's own et-sha'ar formula rather than this connective and is not part of that count), excluded as a boundary candidate on the station criterion alone since no gate name is introduced there. With no gate name introduced anywhere across the span, it closes at 3:12's distinctive family notice for Shallum, שַׁלּוּם֙ בֶּן הַלּוֹחֵ֔שׁ ... ה֖וּא וּבְנוֹתָֽיו (WEB “he and his daughters made repairs.”) — a participant detail not repeated at any other entry in this part's register rows, before the valley gate opens the next station at 3:13.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 3:11's 'second portion' notice (a phrase recurring for several builders later in the chapter) is possible, but that phrase marks a builder's second assignment, not a new gate, and carries no connective of its own to compete with a real seam -- so it does not carry the tier-1 weight a station boundary requires.

boundary_rationale: This single verse is bounded on both sides by named-gate restarts: it opens with אֵת֩ שַׁ֨עַר הַגַּ֜יְא הֶחֱזִ֣יק חָנוּן֮ (WEB “Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the valley gate.”), distinct from 3:12's family notice, and closes by naming the next station as a distance marker rather than a repair ("one thousand cubits of the wall to the dung gate"), so the entry's own repair notice does not extend into 3:14, where the dung gate opens its own station. Hanun and Zanoah's builders receive no chain-connective (acharav/al-yado) of their own, marking this as a complete, self-contained station rather than a link in the preceding or following chain.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 3:13 with 3:14 as one 'gate approach' unit is possible since both concern the same stretch of wall, but each verse carries its own distinct named gate and repair notice, satisfying the station-per-row test independently.

boundary_rationale: Malchijah's dung-gate entry, וְאֵ֣ת שַׁ֣עַר הָאַשְׁפּ֗וֹת הֶחֱזִיק֙ מַלְכִּיָּ֣ה (WEB “Malchijah the son of Rechab, the ruler of the district of Beth Haccherem, repaired the dung gate.”), is a complete builder notice (doors, bolts, bars) marked as a fresh station by its own named gate, distinct from 3:13's valley gate, and further set off by the district-official title sar pelekh Beit-hakkerem attached to Malchijah's name -- a title formula that recurs unevenly through the register but is absent from 3:13's entry (Hanun and the men of Zanoah carry no such title). It closes before the spring/fountain gate opens the next named station at 3:15.
strongest_rejected_alternative: 3:14 and 3:15 are in fact doubly paired -- by the unqualified sar pelekh title (sweep: 2 book-wide, confined to these two verses) and by the matching yiqtol builder notice hu yivnennu (sweep: 2 book-wide, against the qatal hemma vanuhu, sweep: 1 book-wide, unique to 3:13) -- so grouping 3:14 forward with the fountain-gate stretch is a genuinely live rival, not merely possible; it is rejected because 3:14 is bounded by its own named gate and complete repair notice, satisfying the per-station cut independently of the shared title and verb form.

boundary_rationale: Shallun's fountain/spring-gate entry opens the station, וְאֵת֩ שַׁ֨עַר הָעַ֜יִן הֶ֠חֱזִיק שַׁלּ֣וּן (3:15, WEB “Shallun the son of Colhozeh, the ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the spring gate.”), (the OSHB extract carries a ketiv/qere pair here, ויעמידו וְיַעֲמִיד֙, morphological and boundary-neutral), extending to the pool of Shelah and the stairs from David's city. No further named gate interrupts the chain across Nehemiah son of Azbuk, the Levites, Bavvai, Ezer, Baruch (3:20, whose entry inserts the singular הֶחֱרָ֧ה before hecheziq, sweep: 1 book-wide, and carries its own ketiv/qere pair on the patronymic, זבי זַכַּ֖י; the immediately preceding entry at 3:19 shifts its own predicate to the piel וַיְחַזֵּ֨ק, so the connective grammar across this stretch is not in fact uniform), Meremoth's second portion (3:21, repeating the builder already named at 3:4 without introducing a fresh gate or class header), the priests of the plain, Benjamin/Hasshub and Azariah, and Binnui, closing at Pedaiah's entry, אַחֲרָ֖יו פְּדָיָ֥ה בֶן פַּרְעֹֽשׁ (WEB “After him Pedaiah the son of Parosh made repairs.”), before the topographic aside about the Nethinim opens a different discourse type at 3:26. Since a mark is cited, front-seam symmetry is disclosed too: samekh (single-witness) marks Neh.3.14 (the front seam, the dung-gate entry), Neh.3.15, Neh.3.16 and Neh.3.17. Samekh (single-witness) continues at Neh.3.18, Neh.3.19, Neh.3.20 and Neh.3.21, and again at Neh.3.25 (Neh.3.22 and Neh.3.24 unmarked); Neh.3.23 alone carries a double samekh (single-witness). All disclosed as tier-3 weak corroboration, driving none of this row's calls.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Subdividing this stretch at 3:21's repeated Meremoth entry (he reappears after already being named at 3:4) is tempting, but no new gate is named there and no class header is introduced, so it is a bare non-station alternation the segmentation rule excludes as a seam -- this holds independent of the connective grammar, which is not in fact uniform across the span (3:19 shifts to the piel vayechazzek; 3:20 inserts the singular hecherah, sweep: 1 book-wide).

boundary_rationale: This short unit is marked off by a discourse-type shift rather than a new gate name: 3:26 drops the chain's hecheziq/banu repair verbs for a dwelling-notice, וְהַ֨נְּתִינִ֔ים הָי֥וּ יֹשְׁבִ֖ים בָּעֹ֑פֶל (WEB “Now the temple servants lived in Ophel, to the place opposite the water gate toward the east”) -- a stative predicate whose force is reduced by the verbless entries immediately preceding it at 3:25. Verse 27's tie to this unit rests on shared Ophel/tower topographic language alone: אַחֲרָ֛יו הֶחֱזִ֥יקוּ הַתְּקֹעִ֖ים מִדָּ֣ה שֵׁנִ֑ית (WEB “After him the Tekoites repaired another portion”), repeating the tower-and-Ophel landmark vocabulary of 3:26. This concedes rather than claims the connective: acharav occurs 14 times book-wide, 13 inside chapter 3, and every one of those 13 resumes the previously named builder rather than a place -- a masculine-singular antecedent that cannot in any case resume the plural ha-netinim of 3:26, so a personal-antecedent reading of 3:27 has to reach back past the aside to Pedaiah at 3:25. The grouping kept here is therefore a minority construal against the register's own 13-for-13 personal usage of this connective, held on topographic grounds alone. The unit closes before 3:28's horse-gate entry resumes the register.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival ties 3:27 to Pedaiah at 3:25 rather than to 3:26, since acharav's dominant register usage (13 of 13 elsewhere in this chapter) resumes a named builder and the masculine-singular suffix cannot resume 3:26's plural netinim; this splits the pair across two rows, 3:26 closing the fountain-gate stretch and 3:27 continuing from 3:25. The grouping kept here rests on 3:27's shared tower-and-Ophel vocabulary with 3:26 alone, held honestly against the connective's own dominant pattern rather than with it.

boundary_rationale: The horse-gate entry opens the unit on a tier-1 word-order restart rather than the register's own repair formula: מֵעַ֣ל שַׁ֣עַר הַסּוּסִ֗ים הֶחֱזִ֨יקוּ֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים (3:28, WEB “Above the horse gate, the priests made repairs, everyone across from his own house.”) fronts a locative prepositional phrase (me'al, "above") ahead of the verb, drops the chain's own connective, and takes a collective priestly subject in place of a named individual -- a complete single-verse restart with no acharav continuation of its own. This fronted-locative-plus-collective-subject shape recurs exactly once more in the register, at 3:32 (sweep: 2 book-wide, oshb:Neh.3.28 and 3.32); there it closes the register by fronting the already-named sheep-gate terminus that opened it at 3:1, while here at 3:28 it opens a station by fronting a gate not yet named in the chain -- the same word-order device serving opposite functions at the register's start and its close. Verses 29-30 continue the ordinary chain: Shemaiah's entry (3:29) opens ve'acharav hecheziq Shema'yah ben-Shechanyah and names him שֹׁמֵ֖ר שַׁ֥עַר הַמִּזְרָֽח (WEB "the keeper of the east gate") in apposition inside that ordinary hecheziq clause, an office title rather than a report that the east gate itself was rebuilt; then Hananiah and Hanun open the next entry with the register's default connective, ketiv/qere אחרי אַחֲרָ֨יו הֶחֱזִ֜יק חֲנַנְיָ֣ה בֶן שֶׁלֶמְיָ֗ה, disclosed per the ketiv/qere inventory, while Meshullam's own entry later in the same verse opens with the plain connective אַחֲרָ֣יו הֶחֱזִ֗יק מְשֻׁלָּם֙, no ketiv/qere of its own. Neither verse takes a gate as the object of the register's own repair formula -- 3:29's east gate appears only inside Shemaiah's appositional office title -- so this stretch folds into the horse gate's station rather than standing as its own seam. The unit closes before Malchijah's entry opens the next station at 3:31.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 3:29's 'keeper of the east gate' title as its own station head is the rival; it is rejected because the title sits in apposition inside an ordinary hecheziq entry rather than as a fresh restart, unlike 3:28's own genuine word-order break.

boundary_rationale: Malchijah's entry opens with the register's default connective, ketiv/qere אחרי אַחֲרָ֣יו (disclosed per the ketiv/qere inventory), plus hecheziq -- identical in shape to 3:29 and 3:30 -- and its gate, נֶ֚גֶד שַׁ֣עַר הַמִּפְקָ֔ד (3:31, WEB "opposite the gate of Hammiphkad and to the ascent of the corner"), sits in a locative neged phrase rather than the register's accusative et-sha'ar construction, so no station-formula restart opens this unit. What ties 3:31 to 3:32 as the register's closing pair is a catchword bond in local adjacency: הַצֹּ֣רְפִ֔י (3:31) and הַצֹּרְפִ֖ים, the defective, article-prefixed spelling of the goldsmith term (sweep: 2 book-wide, 3:31/3:32; the term itself, including the plene spelling at oshb:Neh.3.8's צֽוֹרְפִ֔ים, sweeps to 3 book-wide, but 3:31/3:32 remain the term's only adjacent pair); and וְהָרֹכְלִ֑ים / וְהָרֹכְלִֽים, the merchant term, sweep: 3 book-wide (3:31, 3:32, and 13:20), likewise adjacent only here. The unit closes with an explicit circuit-completion notice: וּבֵ֨ין עֲלִיַּ֤ת הַפִּנָּה֙ לְשַׁ֣עַר הַצֹּ֔אן (3:32, WEB “Between the ascent of the corner and the sheep gate, the goldsmiths and the merchants made repairs.”) — naming the sheep gate again, the same station that opened the register at 3:1, a tier-1 closural inclusio marking the circuit as complete. This entry shares its own word-order device with 3:28's horse-gate restart -- a fronted locative phrase, no chain connective, and a collective subject in place of a named individual (sweep: 2 book-wide for the shape, oshb:Neh.3.28 and 3.32) -- but here the fronted phrase names the sheep gate already opened at 3:1 rather than a fresh station, so the same device closes the circuit instead of opening one. This is the part's final row; the memoir voice does not resume until the vayehi ka'asher opposition frame beginning MT 3:33 (WEB 4:1), outside this part's range.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row into MT 3:33ff (WEB 4:1ff) on the ground that the register's final wall-completion notice logically anticipates the next opposition cycle is out of scope for this part, which argues just its own edge; the sheep-gate closural naming at 3:32 is sufficient on its own to end the register here.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens on the frame “וַיְהִ֞י כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר שָׁמַ֣ע סַנְבַלַּ֗ט כִּֽי אֲנַ֤חְנוּ…” (vayehi ka'asher shama Sanballat, gloss: 'when Sanballat heard…'), one of eight book-wide members of this frame family (sweep: 8 book-wide skeleton hits for vayehi ka'asher). Function, not family membership, governs each member: this instance and oshb:Neh.4.1 (WEB 4:7) and oshb:Neh.6.1 open opposition-hearing episodes -- two others besides this row's own -- oshb:Neh.4.9 and oshb:Neh.6.16 are outcome-resolution clauses closing an arc already underway, oshb:Neh.7.1 and oshb:Neh.13.19 open non-opposition episodes, and oshb:Neh.4.6 (WEB 4:12) is a report notice whose opener-vs-interior function is argued locally at its own row rather than assumed from family membership. WEB renders the opening “But when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he was angry” (web:Neh.4.1), and the participant set -- Sanballat, joined by Tobiah at oshb:Neh.3.35, addressing 'his brothers and the army of Samaria' -- is narrower than the five-party coalition that opens the next episode at oshb:Neh.4.1 (WEB 4:7), which is the strongest signal that a new unit starts there rather than continuing this one. Sanballat's taunt (oshb:Neh.3.34, “וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לִפְנֵ֣י אֶחָ֗יו וְחֵיל֙ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מָ֛ה הַיְּהוּדִ֥ים הָאֲמֵלָלִ֖ים עֹשִׂ֑ים הֲיַעַזְב֨וּ לָהֶ֤ם הֲיִזְבָּ֨חוּ֙ הַיְכַלּ֣וּ בַיּ֔וֹם הַיְחַיּ֧וּ אֶת הָאֲבָנִ֛ים מֵעֲרֵמ֥וֹת הֶעָפָ֖ר וְהֵ֥מָּה שְׂרוּפֽוֹת”) and Tobiah's jibe (oshb:Neh.3.35, “וְטוֹבִיָּ֥ה הָעַמֹּנִ֖י אֶצְל֑וֹ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר גַּ֚ם אֲשֶׁר…”, gloss: 'even what they are building—if a fox climbed up it') escalate into direct address to God at oshb:Neh.3.36, “שְׁמַ֤ע אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ כִּֽי…” (gloss: 'hear, our God, for…'), the shema eloheinu taunt-prayer. Per the strategy's inset policy this prayer (WEB 4:4-5) stays inside its host episode: its opening vocative shifts address-mode but nothing marks an independent RETURN to narrative on its far side—oshb:Neh.3.38 simply resumes the wayyiqtol chain the episode was already running (“וַנִּבְנֶה֙ אֶת הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה וַתִּקָּשֵׁ֥ר כָּל הַחוֹמָ֖ה עַד חֶצְיָ֑הּ וַיְהִ֧י לֵ֦ב לָעָ֖ם לַעֲשֽׂוֹת”, WEB: “So we built the wall… for the people had a mind to work”, web:Neh.4.6), so the inset is framed on one side alone and does not earn its own row. That building notice is the unit's proper close: it reports outcome (half-height, morale intact) before the next vayehi ka'asher frame reopens the conflict. A PE mark follows oshb:Neh.3.32 (petuchah, single-witness), the seam this part inherits from the prior wall-register; PE also follows oshb:Neh.3.35 (petuchah, single-witness) (WEB 4:3), sitting just before the prayer inset, and oshb:Neh.3.38 (petuchah, single-witness) (WEB 4:6) closes the unit—all three disclosed together per symmetry, all tier-3 weak, none driving the call.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating oshb:Neh.3.36-37 (WEB 4:4-5) as its own inset row loses because the prayer's opening vocative has no matching bilateral tier-1 marker on its far side, where the text simply resumes ordinary narrative.

boundary_rationale: “וַיְהִ֣י כַאֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמַ֣ע סַנְבַלַּ֡ט וְ֠טוֹבִיָּה…” (vayehi ka'asher shama Sanballat veToviyah, gloss: 'when Sanballat, Tobiah… heard') reopens the vayehi ka'asher family (oshb:Neh.4.1, WEB 4:7 -- one of the family's three function-verified opposition-hearing openers, alongside oshb:Neh.3.33 and oshb:Neh.6.1) with an expanded, five-party coalition ('the Arabians, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites' per web:Neh.4.7) that marks a new escalation distinct from the two-man mockery just closed. The threat moves from words to action—“וַיִּקְשְׁר֤וּ כֻלָּם֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו לָב֖וֹא לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְלַעֲשׂ֥וֹת ל֖וֹ תּוֹעָֽה” (gloss: 'they all conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem and cause it confusion’)—and draws the memoir's own countermove, “וַנִּתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַנַּעֲמִ֨יד מִשְׁמָ֧ר עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יוֹמָ֥ם וָלַ֖יְלָה מִפְּנֵיהֶֽם” (gloss: 'we prayed to our God, and set a watch against them day and night because of them’), rendered by WEB as “But we made our prayer to our God, and set a watch against them day and night because of them” (web:Neh.4.9). The unit closes with two quoted voices of alarm, Judah's discouragement (4.10, “וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָ֗ה כָּשַׁל֙ כֹּ֣חַ הַסַּבָּ֔ל וְהֶעָפָ֖ר הַרְבֵּ֑ה וַאֲנַ֨חְנוּ֙ לֹ֣א נוּכַ֔ל לִבְנ֖וֹת בַּחוֹמָֽה”) and the adversaries' threat (4.11, “וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ צָרֵ֗ינוּ לֹ֤א יֵדְעוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִרְא֔וּ עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁר נָב֥וֹא אֶל תּוֹכָ֖ם וַהֲרַגְנ֑וּם וְהִשְׁבַּ֖תְנוּ אֶת הַמְּלָאכָֽה”), both introduced by vayomer/vayomeru—a matched pair of reported speech that ends the anxiety report before third parties (the Jews living nearby) bring a fresh warning at the next frame (oshb:Neh.4.6, WEB 4:12).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 4:7-15 into one row (as the strategy's block map names it) loses granularity: the participant shift at 4:12 ('the Jews who lived by them') is a distinct source of alarm from the international coalition of 4:7-11, and treating all nine verses as one unit obscures that shift.

boundary_rationale: “וַֽיְהִי֙ כַּאֲשֶׁר בָּ֣אוּ הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים אֶצְלָ֑ם…” (vayehi ka'asher ba'u ha-yehudim ha-yoshvim etzlam, gloss: 'when the Jews who lived by them came’) opens a third instance of the frame (oshb:Neh.4.6, WEB 4:12) with a new informant class (local kin, not the coalition of 4:7-11), reporting WEB's tenfold refrain “Wherever you turn, they will attack us” (web:Neh.4.12). Nehemiah's guard deployment answers directly, “וָֽאַעֲמִ֞יד מִֽתַּחְתִּיּ֧וֹת לַמָּק֛וֹם מֵאַחֲרֵ֥י לַחוֹמָ֖ה בצחחיים בַּצְּחִיחִ֑ים וָֽאַעֲמִ֤יד…” (gloss: 'I stationed [guards] in the lowest parts’; the oshb extract carries the ketiv בצחחיים beside the qere בַּצְּחִיחִ֑ים here, disclosed per the ketiv/qere inventory), then his speech to the nobles, “וָאֵ֣רֶא וָאָק֗וּם וָאֹמַ֞ר אֶל הַחֹרִ֤ים וְאֶל הַסְּגָנִים֙ וְאֶל יֶ֣תֶר הָעָ֔ם אַל תִּֽירְא֖וּ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם אֶת אֲדֹנָ֞י הַגָּד֤וֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא֙ זְכֹ֔רוּ וְהִֽלָּחֲמ֗וּ עַל אֲחֵיכֶם֙ בְּנֵיכֶ֣ם וּבְנֹתֵיכֶ֔ם נְשֵׁיכֶ֖ם וּבָתֵּיכֶֽם…” (gloss: 'I saw, and rose up, and said to the nobles, the rulers, and the rest of the people: don't be afraid of them; remember the Lord, great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your houses’). The row closes with the resolution notice “וַיְהִ֞י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר שָׁמְע֤וּ אוֹיְבֵ֨ינוּ֙ כִּי נ֣וֹדַֽע לָ֔נוּ וַיָּ֥פֶר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת עֲצָתָ֑ם ונשוב וַנָּ֤שָׁב כֻּלָּ֨נוּ֙ אֶל הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה אִ֖ישׁ אֶל מְלַאכְתּֽוֹ” (gloss: 'when our enemies heard… God had brought their counsel to nothing, and we all returned to the wall’; ketiv ונשוב/qere וַנָּ֤שָׁב disclosed), WEB “When our enemies heard that it was known to us, and God had brought their counsel to nothing, all of us returned to the wall, everyone to his work” (web:Neh.4.15). This row's own close holds independent of how 4:15 attaches to what follows: oshb:Neh.4.9 (WEB 4:15) resolves with its own divine-agency clause (vayafer ha-Elohim et-atzatam, 'God had brought their counsel to nothing'), a resolution shape shared with oshb:Neh.6.16 (va-yed'u ki me-et Eloheinu, 'they perceived that this work was done by our God'). The hearing-subject form 'our enemies' (oyveinu) itself sweeps to 4 book-wide (oshb:Neh.4.9, 5.9, 6.1 [defective spelling, no vav], 6.16), and three of those four sit inside the vayehi-ka'asher family proper (4.9, 6.1, 6.16; 5.9's oyveinu falls in an unrelated construction, 'the reproach of the nations, our enemies', outside the family) -- but membership in that sub-shape does not by itself settle function: oshb:Neh.6.1 shares the same hearing-subject yet opens its own unit rather than resolving one, so it is the divine-agency clause specifically, not membership in the hearing-subject sub-shape, that marks 4.9/4:15 and 6:16 as resolvers. A PE mark (single-witness) sits at MT 4.8, interior to this row's own span (WEB 4:14, one verse before the close); tier-3 weak corroboration, available in principle to the reading that opens the next unit at 4:15 rather than to this row's own close, and not decisive for either. The following unit is independently self-opening at MT 4.10 (WEB 4:16), which carries its own temporal frame ('from that day on'), so 4:16-23 needs nothing from 4:15 to open it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 4:15 (oshb 4.9) as the opener of the next unit (with 4:16-23) remains a genuinely contestable rival, engaged rather than dismissed: 4:9/4:15 shares its hearing-subject and vayehi-ka'asher shape with 6:1, a member that opens rather than resolves, so shared membership alone cannot settle which function 4:15 performs. This row's own close rests instead on 4:9's divine-agency resolution clause -- the same shape carried at 6:16, per the two-resolver split above -- and on 4:16's own independent self-opening temporal frame, so 4:16-23 does not need 4:15 to open it even if 4:15 could in principle be read either way.

boundary_rationale: The opening “וַיְהִ֣י מִן הַיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא…” (vayehi min-hayom hahu, gloss: 'and it was from that day forth’; oshb:Neh.4.10, WEB 4:16) is a different temporal formula from the vayehi ka'asher family that structures the rest of the chapter: it opens a shift from perfective episode-narration to habitual/participial description ('half of my servants did the work, and half of them held the spears…', web:Neh.4.16), a discourse-level change that outlasts any single incident and describes the STANDING practice through to the chapter's end. The unit's close is chapter 4's closing verse: “So neither I, nor my brothers, nor my servants… took off our clothes” (web:Neh.4.23), a summary clause with no further frame following it before Nehemiah's economic material opens a wholly different register in ch.5. A SAMEKH mark follows oshb:Neh.4.17 (samekh, single-witness) (WEB 4:23), that same closing verse, weak corroboration for the ch.4/ch.5 division that this row's close already coincides with on textual grounds. A PE mark also sits at oshb:Neh.4.8 (petuchah, single-witness) (WEB 4:14), immediately before the rival's own proposed head at MT 4:9 (WEB 4:15); disclosed here as the matching tier-3 weak corroboration for that rival, symmetric with the mark already disclosed at 4:17 above, and likewise driving none of this row's calls. The closer rival sits one verse earlier: MT 4:9 (web:Neh.4.15 = oshb:Neh.4.9) is itself a vayehi ka'asher frame member, “וַיְהִ֞י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר שָׁמְע֤וּ אוֹיְבֵ֨ינוּ֙ כִּי נ֣וֹדַֽע לָ֔נוּ וַיָּ֥פֶר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת עֲצָתָ֑ם ונשוב וַנָּ֤שָׁב כֻּלָּ֨נוּ֙ אֶל הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה אִ֖ישׁ אֶל מְלַאכְתּֽוֹ” (gloss: 'when our enemies heard that it was known to us... every man to his work'), closing on the same melakhah root this unit is built on, so 4:15's return-to-work reads as continuous with 4:16's elaboration rather than as a closed prior scene; this join, not the 4:22 seam below, is the row's most contestable edge. The habitual/participial texture is also not uniform throughout: MT 4:16 (web:Neh.4.22 = oshb:Neh.4.16), “גַּ֣ם בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ אָמַ֣רְתִּי לָעָ֔ם אִ֣ישׁ וְנַעֲר֔וֹ יָלִ֖ינוּ בְּת֣וֹךְ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְהָֽיוּ לָ֧נוּ הַלַּ֛יְלָה מִשְׁמָ֖ר וְהַיּ֥וֹם מְלָאכָֽה” (gloss: 'moreover at that time I said to the people...'), opens on gam plus a qatal 1cs speech verb, and MT 4:17 returns to a nominal clause; the shared mishmar/melakhah vocabulary spanning 4:16-17 binds that interior shift back into the unit, not verb-form uniformity. The gam-plus-temporal shape itself is not unit-demarcating on its own: it recurs at four verse-initial, unprefixed occurrences book-wide (sweep: 4, MT 4.16 [this row], 5.14, 6.17, 13.23), of which this row's own 4:16 sits interior to a single unit rather than opening a fresh one; MT 5:13's own gam, by contrast, opens on a possessed noun and a plain qatal verb with no temporal phrase at all and is not itself a member of this shape.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The stronger rival is a Neh.4.15-Neh.4.23 unit headed by MT 4:9's own vayehi ka'asher frame and melakhah-rooted close (web:Neh.4.15 = oshb:Neh.4.9); it is engaged rather than dismissed, since the 4:15/4:16 join is genuinely contestable, but the discourse-mode pivot at min-hayom hahu and the mishmar/melakhah envelope binding 4:16-23 keep the row's own span intact.

boundary_rationale: A wholly new register opens with “וַתְּהִ֨י צַעֲקַ֥ת הָעָ֛ם וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם גְּדוֹלָ֑ה אֶל אֲחֵיהֶ֖ם הַיְּהוּדִֽים” (vatehi tza'akat ha'am … gedolah, gloss: 'and there arose a great cry of the people’), WEB “Then there arose a great cry of the people and of their wives against their brothers the Jews” (web:Neh.5.1)—a different opening formula from the vayehi ka'asher family that governed all of ch.4, and a hard topic break from the wall-guard arrangement just closed. Three matched complaints follow, each opened “וְיֵשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֹמְרִ֔ים בָּנֵ֥ינוּ וּבְנֹתֵ֖ינוּ…” / “וְיֵשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֹמְרִ֔ים שְׂדֹתֵ֛ינוּ וּכְרָמֵ֥ינוּ…” / “וְיֵשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֹמְרִ֔ים לָוִ֥ינוּ כֶ֖סֶף…” (ve-yesh asher omrim, gloss in each case 'and there were [some] who said'; sweep: 3 book-wide skeleton hits, all three at 5.2-5.4), an anaphoric list device escalating from grain shortage to mortgaged fields to royal-tribute debt. The climax breaks the anaphora's pattern: “וְעַתָּ֗ה כִּבְשַׂ֤ר אַחֵ֨ינוּ֙ בְּשָׂרֵ֔נוּ כִּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם…” (ve'atah kivsar acheinu besarenu, gloss: 'yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brothers'), WEB “Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brothers… we bring our sons and our daughters into bondage” (web:Neh.5.5), closing the complaint register before Nehemiah's own reaction opens the next unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 5:1-13 as one long reform narrative (per the strategy's block map) is defensible but flattens the anaphoric ve-yesh asher omrim register (5:2-4) and its ve'atah-marked climax (5:5) into an undifferentiated span longer than this book's typical narrative unit.

boundary_rationale: “וַיִּ֥חַר לִ֖י מְאֹ֑ד כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ אֶת זַֽעֲקָתָ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה” (vayichar li me'od ka'asher shama'ti, gloss: 'and I was very angry when I heard’) opens Nehemiah's personal reaction (web:Neh.5.6, “I was very angry when I heard their cry and these words”), a hinge that answers 5:1-5's complaint register with Nehemiah's own voiced response rather than continuing the anaphoric list. He states the charge directly, “וַיִּמָּלֵ֨ךְ לִבִּ֜י עָלַ֗י וָאָרִ֨יבָה֙ אֶת הַחֹרִ֣ים וְאֶת הַסְּגָנִ֔ים וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָהֶ֔ם מַשָּׁ֥א אִישׁ בְּאָחִ֖יו אַתֶּ֣ם נשאים נֹשִׁ֑ים וָאֶתֵּ֥ן עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם קְהִלָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה” (gloss: 'you exact usury, each on his brother’; the oshb extract carries the ketiv נשאים beside the qere נֹשִׁ֑ים here, disclosed per the ketiv/qere inventory), then confronts the nobles in assembly. The unit closes on a clean silence-marker: “וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָהֶ֗ם אֲנַ֣חְנוּ קָ֠נִינוּ אֶת אַחֵ֨ינוּ הַיְּהוּדִ֜ים הַנִּמְכָּרִ֤ים לַגּוֹיִם֙ כְּדֵ֣י בָ֔נוּ וְגַם אַתֶּ֛ם תִּמְכְּר֥וּ אֶת אֲחֵיכֶ֖ם וְנִמְכְּרוּ לָ֑נוּ וַֽיַּחֲרִ֔ישׁוּ וְלֹ֥א מָצְא֖וּ דָּבָֽר”, WEB “Then they held their peace, and found not a word to say” (web:Neh.5.8)— closing the confrontation with its own complete turn-sequence: challenge, then silence (וַֽיַּחֲרִ֔ישׁוּ, itself unique to this verse book-wide: sweep 1, oshb:Neh.5.8), then no reply. This closing turn-sequence is sufficient on its own; it does not depend on any claim about 5:9, whose own opening (ketiv vayomer / qere va'omar, with no addressee) is in any case a distinct form from this row's own repeated וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָהֶ֗ם (va'omrah lahem, 'I said to them,' at 5:7 and 5:8) rather than a recurrence of it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Running 5:6-13 together as a single confrontation-to-resolution arc remains a live alternative: 5:9 does switch speech-verb form (va'omar, replacing this row's own va'omrah lahem), but that switch is not treated as independently decisive; it is resisted here because 5:8's own closing turn-sequence -- challenge, silence, no reply -- is a complete transaction in its own right, the strongest signal either side of this seam offers.

boundary_rationale: The row opens on “ויאמר וָאוֹמַ֕ר לֹא ט֥וֹב הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּ֣ם עֹשִׂ֑ים הֲל֞וֹא בְּיִרְאַ֤ת אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ תֵּלֵ֔כוּ מֵחֶרְפַּ֖ת הַגּוֹיִ֥ם אוֹיְבֵֽינוּ” (gloss: 'the thing that you do is not good; shouldn't you walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the nations, our enemies?'): the OSHB extract's unpointed ketiv (vayomer, 3ms, 'and he said') sits beside the pointed qere (va'omar, 1cs, 'and I said') -- a person alternation, not a bare spelling variant -- following the silence that closed 5:8 (oshb:Neh.5.8, samekh, single-witness, marking the same seam from its far side). The opening edge does not rest on the qere's reintroduced speaker alone: 5:9 itself switches speech-verb form, to va'omar with no addressee, replacing the preceding row's own va'omrah lahem ('I said to them') at 5:7 and 5:8; what changes at 5:9 is the speech-act itself, from confrontation ('you exact usury') to reform demand ('the thing that you do is not good'), a content shift the ketiv reading does not disturb either way. Nehemiah's demand (“הָשִׁיבוּ֩ נָ֨א לָהֶ֜ם כְּהַיּ֗וֹם שְׂדֹתֵיהֶ֛ם כַּרְמֵיהֶ֥ם…”, gloss: 'restore to them, please, this very day’, WEB “Please restore to them, even today, their fields”, web:Neh.5.11) draws the nobles' agreement (“וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ נָשִׁ֗יב וּמֵהֶם֙ לֹ֣א נְבַקֵּ֔שׁ כֵּ֣ן נַעֲשֶׂ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר…”, gloss: 'we will restore, and require nothing from them’) and Nehemiah's oath of the priests. The unit closes with the enacted ceremony, “גַּם חָצְנִ֣י נָעַ֗רְתִּי וָֽאֹמְרָ֡ה כָּ֣כָה יְנַעֵ֪ר הָֽאֱלֹהִ֟ים אֶת כָּל הָאִישׁ֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא יָקִ֜ים אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה מִבֵּיתוֹ֙ וּמִ֣יגִיע֔וֹ וְכָ֛כָה יִהְיֶ֥ה נָע֖וּר וָרֵ֑ק וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ כָֽל הַקָּהָ֜ל אָמֵ֗ן וַֽיְהַלְלוּ֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָעָ֖ם כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה”, WEB “All the assembly said, "Amen," and praised Yahweh. The people did according to this promise” (web:Neh.5.13)—a complete demand-response-ratification transaction with its own closural 'Amen' before the memoir aside on the governor's allowance opens new material at 5:14.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the reform demand (5:9-11) from the oath ceremony (5:12-13) is possible but weaker: the demand-response-ratification sequence reads as one transactional unit, and the interior seam at 5:11/12 carries a bare speaker alternation but no tier-1 marker.

boundary_rationale: “גַּ֞ם מִיּ֣וֹם אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֣ה אֹתִ֗י לִהְי֣וֹת פֶּחָם֮ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ…” (gam miyom asher tzivah oti lihyot pecha, gloss: 'moreover, from the day that he appointed me to be their governor’) opens a retrospective aside spanning Nehemiah's whole twelve-year tenure ('from the twentieth year even to the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes', web:Neh.5.14)—a scope no single scene in 5:1-13 shares and the actual opening signal: the gam-prefixed opener by itself is not sufficient to carry the edge (the unprefixed, temporal gam shape recurs at four verse-initial instances book-wide -- sweep: 4, oshb:Neh.4.16, 5.14, 6.17, 13.23 -- and two of the other three, 6:17 and 13:23, themselves open fresh units, while the third, MT 4:16 = web:Neh.4.22, sits interior to the opposition-cycle unit that precedes ch.5), so the shape is disclosed here only as corroboration, not as the sole driver of the fresh unit; the twelve-year retrospective scope-shift itself is what carries the edge. The aside closes on “זָכְרָה לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י לְטוֹבָ֑ה כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֖יתִי עַל הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה”, WEB “Remember me, my God, for all the good that I have done for this people” (web:Neh.5.19)—the FIRST occurrence of the zokrah-li elohai refrain (sweep: 6 book-wide skeleton hits for zochrah; first of the six at 5.19), which the strategy identifies as this book's regular memoir unit-closer. A PE mark follows oshb:Neh.5.19 (petuchah, single-witness), chapter 5's closing verse, weak corroboration for the close already secured by the refrain.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 5:14-19 as a continuation of the reform narrative (rather than its own retrospective aside) is the strategy's own flagged low-confidence question, but the twelve-year scope and the zokrah-closer both argue for a separate unit here.

boundary_rationale: “וַיְהִ֣י כַאֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁמַ֣ע לְסַנְבַלַּ֣ט וְ֠טוֹבִיָּה וּלְגֶ֨שֶׁם הָֽעַרְבִ֜י וּלְיֶ֣תֶר…” (vayehi ka'asher nishma le-Sanballat, gloss: 'when it was reported to Sanballat’) is the passive-niphal variant of the vayehi-ka'asher opener (sweep: 8 book-wide skeleton hits for vayehi ka'asher; oshb:Neh.6.1 among them) and returns the intrigue material to the frame family after the memoir aside of 5:14-19. It introduces a new list of enemies including Geshem, and a new grievance ('the wall was built', web:Neh.6.1) distinct from the wall-still-under-construction anxiety of ch.4. Sanballat's meeting proposal is refused four times in an explicit counted formula: “וַיִּשְׁלְח֥וּ אֵלַ֛י כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה אַרְבַּ֣ע פְּעָמִ֑ים וָאָשִׁ֥יב אוֹתָ֖ם כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה”, WEB “They sent to me four times like this; and I answered them the same way” (web:Neh.6.4)—a self-closing numbered refrain. MT 6:5 continues the identical count one further step ('the fifth time', web:Neh.6.5), and MT 6:7's own closing invitation, “וְעַתָּ֣ה לְכָ֔ה וְנִֽוָּעֲצָ֖ה יַחְדָּֽו”, differs from MT 6:2's “לְכָ֞ה וְנִֽוָּעֲדָ֥ה יַחְדָּ֛ו” by a single root consonant (yod-ayin-dalet at 6:2, yod-ayin-tsade at 6:7; each of these two specific cohortative forms sweeps: 1 book-wide). The yod-ayin-dalet root of 6:2 itself recurs once more, at MT 6:10 (root sweep: 2 book-wide, 6:2 and 6:10; the string also surfaces inside the proper name No'adyah at 6:14, a substring artefact, not a further occurrence of the root in use), but there it is Shemaiah, not Sanballat, proposing -- "let us meet in the house of God, within the temple" -- with neither lekhah nor yachdav and a different addressee and setting, so it echoes the root rather than extending the lekhah-yachdav demand itself. Even so, the meeting proposal in its original lekhah-yachdav shape runs continuously from 6:2 through 6:7 rather than ending at 6:4. What closes here is the channel and audience: the private, four-times-repeated oral invitation to a face-to-face meeting gives way at 6:5 to an unsealed letter carried by a servant, escalating from a private trap to a public accusation. The count-formula's own continuation into 'the fifth time' is a real signal against a hard break at exactly this seam, weighing this row's confidence down from what a clean four-times refrain alone would support.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 6:1-9 as one continuous 'fifth time' sequence is real counter-pressure, since 6:5 extends the identical count and the lekhah-yachdav meeting demand itself continues, with only a one-consonant root variant, into 6:7; the boundary is retained here only on the change of channel and audience (private oral invitation to public open letter), not on any change in the demand's content, and that narrower warrant carries the seam on its own.

boundary_rationale: “וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ אֵלַ֨י סַנְבַלַּ֜ט כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֛ה פַּ֥עַם חֲמִישִׁ֖ית אֶֽת נַעֲר֑וֹ וְאִגֶּ֥רֶת פְּתוּחָ֖ה בְּיָדֽוֹ”, WEB “Sanballat sent his servant to me the same way the fifth time with an open letter in his hand” (web:Neh.6.5), opens on a changed channel and audience -- an unsealed letter carried by a servant, a public accusation of rebellion and kingship (quoted at “כָּת֣וּב בָּ֗הּ בַּגּוֹיִ֤ם נִשְׁמָע֙ וְגַשְׁמ֣וּ אֹמֵ֔ר אַתָּ֤ה וְהַיְּהוּדִים֙…”) -- rather than on any change in the demand itself: MT 6:7's own closing clause, “וְעַתָּ֣ה לְכָ֔ה וְנִֽוָּעֲצָ֖ה יַחְדָּֽו”, is the same lekhah-yachdav meeting invitation as MT 6:2's “לְכָ֞ה וְנִֽוָּעֲדָ֥ה יַחְדָּ֛ו”, one root consonant apart (the same 6:2/6:7 contrast already drawn for the adjoining unit, Neh.6.1-Neh.6.4), and MT 6:6's niphal נִשְׁמָע echoes the same niphal opening MT 6:1. A SAMEKH follows oshb:Neh.6.7 (samekh, single-witness), interior to this span between the letter's quoted content and Nehemiah's reply; tier-3 and non-driving, disclosed here for symmetry with this cluster's other rows. Nehemiah's flat denial, “וָאֶשְׁלְחָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֤א נִֽהְיָה֙ כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֖ר אַתָּ֣ה אוֹמֵ֑ר כִּ֥י מִֽלִּבְּךָ֖ אַתָּ֥ה בוֹדָֽאם” (gloss: 'no such things have been done as you say’, WEB “There are no such things done as you say, but you imagine them out of your own heart”, web:Neh.6.8), and the closing aside “כִּ֣י כֻלָּ֗ם מְיָֽרְאִ֤ים אוֹתָ֨נוּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יִרְפּ֧וּ יְדֵיהֶ֛ם מִן הַמְּלָאכָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א תֵעָשֶׂ֑ה וְעַתָּ֖ה חַזֵּ֥ק אֶת יָדָֽי”, WEB “But now, strengthen my hands” (web:Neh.6.9), stay inside this episode as a prayer-like petition rather than an isolated inset, its imperative, חַזֵּ֥ק אֶת יָדָֽי, is a book-wide singleton (sweep: 1, Neh.6.9 only) with no independent re-entry marker of its own, so nothing detaches it from the surrounding narrative. The next verse pivots to a wholly new informant (Shemaiah) and a new plot type (temple entrapment), closing this unit here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating 6:9b ('strengthen my hands') as its own prayer-inset row loses under the inset rule: its imperative opens with no answering re-entry marker, and the episode just continues into 6:10 unbroken.

boundary_rationale: “וַאֲנִי בָ֗אתִי בֵּ֣ית שְֽׁמַֽעְיָ֧ה בֶן דְּלָיָ֛ה בֶּן מְהֵֽיטַבְאֵ֖ל וְה֣וּא עָצ֑וּר” (va'ani vati beit Shema'yah, gloss: 'and I went to the house of Shemaiah, who was shut up') opens with a new named informant and a new location -- the house of Shemaiah, where Nehemiah goes; the temple precinct enters only inside Shemaiah's own proposal, “וַיֹּ֡אמֶר נִוָּעֵד֩ אֶל בֵּ֨ית הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶל תּ֣וֹךְ הַֽהֵיכָ֗ל” (gloss: 'let us meet in the house of God, inside the temple'), a niphal proposal verb continuing the same meeting-demand chain opened at MT 6:2 (לְכָ֞ה וְנִֽוָּעֲדָ֥ה) and echoed at MT 6:7 (לְכָ֔ה וְנִֽוָּעֲצָ֖ה): 2 genuine verbal instances of the root at MT 6:2 and 6:10 (a third skeleton hit at MT 6:14 is the proper name Noadiah, a false positive), a chain running across both the 6:4/6:5 and 6:9/6:10 seams. That continuity is the reason this episode reads as a fresh scene rather than a fresh proposal: what changes at 6:10 is not the demand-chain but the venue and the informant, moving from a written exchange to an in-person entrapment staged by a named intermediary. Nehemiah's refusal, “וָאֹמְרָ֗ה הַאִ֤ישׁ כָּמ֨וֹנִי֙ יִבְרָ֔ח וּמִ֥י כָמ֛וֹנִי אֲשֶׁר יָב֥וֹא אֶל הַהֵיכָ֖ל וָחָ֑י לֹ֖א אָבֽוֹא”, WEB “Should a man like me flee?… I will not go in” (web:Neh.6.11), and his discernment, “וָאַכִּ֕ירָה וְהִנֵּ֥ה לֹֽא אֱלֹהִ֖ים שְׁלָח֑וֹ כִּ֤י הַנְּבוּאָה֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר עָלַ֔י וְטוֹבִיָּ֥ה וְסַנְבַלַּ֖ט שְׂכָרֽוֹ” (gloss: 'and I perceived that God had not sent him’), unmask the hired-prophet scheme. A PE mark follows oshb:Neh.6.13 (petuchah, single-witness), sitting at the alternative 6:13/6:14 division rather than this row's own chosen close; tier-3 and non-driving, it is disclosed here for symmetry regardless of which reading it happens to sit nearest. The unit closes with the hostile zokrah, “זָכְרָ֧ה אֱלֹהַ֛י לְטוֹבִיָּ֥ה וּלְסַנְבַלַּ֖ט כְּמַעֲשָׂ֣יו אֵ֑לֶּה וְגַ֨ם לְנוֹעַדְיָ֤ה הַנְּבִיאָה֙ וּלְיֶ֣תֶר הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ מְיָֽרְאִ֥ים אוֹתִֽי”, WEB “Remember, my God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to these their works… and the rest of the prophets that would have put me in fear” (web:Neh.6.14)—the second of the book's six zokrah instances (sweep: 6 book-wide skeleton hits) and, per the strategy's own device matrix, this book's regular memoir unit-closing device, ending the whole 6:1-14 intrigues super-unit before the completion notice opens at 6:15.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the Shemaiah narrative (6:10-13) from its zokrah close (6:14) into two rows loses the device's function: zokrah closes memoir units in this book rather than opening new ones, so it belongs with what precedes.

boundary_rationale: The preceding unit's own close licenses a fresh start here: “זָכְרָ֧ה אֱלֹהַ֛י לְטוֹבִיָּ֥ה וּלְסַנְבַלַּ֖ט כְּמַעֲשָׂ֣יו אֵ֑לֶּה” (oshb:Neh.6.14), the second of the book's six-member zokrah family (sweep: 6 book-wide skeleton hits) and this book's regular tier-1 memoir unit-closing device, so the dated notice that follows opens on a clean slate rather than mid-unit. “וַתִּשְׁלַם֙ הַֽחוֹמָ֔ה בְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה לֶאֱל֑וּל לַחֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּשְׁנַ֖יִם יֽוֹם”, WEB “So the wall was finished in the twenty-fifth day of Elul, in fifty-two days” (web:Neh.6.15), is a dated achievement notice using a different verb (vatishlam, 'was finished') from the vayehi ka'asher frame, closing the building project that has run since ch.3. “וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר שָֽׁמְעוּ֙ כָּל א֣וֹיְבֵ֔ינוּ וַיִּֽרְא֗וּ כָּל הַגּוֹיִם֙…” (vayehi ka'asher sham'u kol-oyveinu, gloss: 'when all our enemies heard of it’; oshb:Neh.6.16) is a further instance of the frame family, but here functioning as the achievement's REACTION-clause ('all the nations… lost their confidence; for they perceived that this work was done by our God', web:Neh.6.16) rather than opening a new adversarial plot, so it is kept paired with 6:15 as one completion-and-response beat rather than split. A PE mark follows oshb:Neh.6.15 (petuchah, single-witness), sitting exactly at the join between these two verses; it is disclosed rather than followed, since the achievement/reaction pairing is a tighter content link than a weak, tier-3 paragraph division can override.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting 6:15 (completion date) from 6:16 (reaction) at the Masoretic petuchah (single-witness) is a live option the mark itself invites, but it separates a cause from its stated effect ('they perceived that this work was done by our God') that the narrative presents as one beat.

boundary_rationale: “גַּ֣ם בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם מַרְבִּ֞ים חֹרֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙…” (gam bayamim hahem, gloss: 'moreover, in those days’), WEB “Moreover in those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah” (web:Neh.6.17), is the same retrospective-notice opener (bayamim hahem) used at 13:23 (sweep: 2 book-wide skeleton hits for bayamim hahem, oshb:Neh.6.17 and oshb:Neh.13.23), distinct from bayamim hahemmah at 13:15; the gam-prefixed, undated aside pulls back from the completion notice's specific 25-Elul date to describe a standing social network. The reciprocal traffic this notice describes closes here: “גַּ֣ם טוֹבֹתָ֗יו הָי֤וּ אֹמְרִים֙ לְפָנַ֔י וּדְבָרַ֕י הָי֥וּ מוֹצִיאִ֖ים ל֑וֹ אִגְּר֛וֹת שָׁלַ֥ח טוֹבִיָּ֖ה לְיָֽרְאֵֽנִי”, WEB “Also they spoke of his good deeds before me, and reported my words to him. Tobiah sent letters to put me in fear” (web:Neh.6.19), before the following unit opens on its own tier-1 frame, “וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר…” (oshb:Neh.7.1), a fresh vayehi ka'asher member rather than a bare chapter break.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 6:17-19 into the 6:15-16 completion notice as one continuous close to the wall project loses the opener's own signal: bayamim hahem marks a distinct, undated retrospective aside, the same device used to open reform notices elsewhere in the book.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens with the book's vayehi-ka'asher episode-frame, "וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר נִבְנְתָה֙ הַחוֹמָ֔ה" (web:Neh.7.1, “Now when the wall was built and I had set up the doors, and the gatekeepers and the singers and the Levites were appointed,”), the same opener-family used for major memoir turns elsewhere in the book (e.g. Neh.4.1, Neh.6.1). The first-person memoir chain that follows -- וָאַעֲמִ֖יד (7:1), וָאֲצַוֶּ֞ה (7:2) -- is itself complicated at 7:3: the OSHB extract's “ויאמר וָאֹמַ֣ר לָהֶ֗ם לֹ֣א יִפָּֽתְח֞וּ שַׁעֲרֵ֤י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ עַד חֹ֣ם הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ וְעַ֨ד הֵ֥ם עֹמְדִ֛ים יָגִ֥יפוּ הַדְּלָת֖וֹת וֶאֱחֹ֑זוּ וְהַעֲמֵ֗יד מִשְׁמְרוֹת֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם אִ֚ישׁ בְּמִשְׁמָר֔וֹ וְאִ֖ישׁ נֶ֥גֶד בֵּיתֽוֹ” carries an unpointed 3ms ketiv (vayomer, 'and he said') beside the pointed 1cs qere (va'omar, 'and I said'); the memoir-voice unity this row leans on holds only on the qere reading. Watch orders to Hanani and Hananiah (Neh.7.2-Neh.7.3) and the disjunctive aside on the city's condition, "וְהָעִ֞יר רַחֲבַ֤ת יָדַ֨יִם֙" (Neh.7.4, "the city was wide and large; but the people were few therein"), supply the practical problem that the closing verse resolves: "וַיִּתֵּ֤ן אֱלֹהַי֙…" (web:Neh.7.5) shares the phrase elohai el libbi with Neh.2.12's "מָ֗ה אֱלֹהַי֙ נֹתֵ֣ן אֶל לִבִּ֔י" (gloss: 'what my God was putting into my heart', embedded participial clause, governed by velo higgadti, וְלֹא הִגַּ֣דְתִּי לְאָדָ֔ם) -- the same motive, not the same construction, since 7:5's is a finite wayyiqtol main clause; each form is quoted here rather than merely cross-referenced, and the unit ends on a citation formula, "וָאֶמְצָ֖א כָּת֥וּב בּֽוֹ" (web:Neh.7.5, “I found this written in it:”), which hands off to the copied document rather than belonging to it. A petuchah follows oshb:Neh.7.5 (single-witness), weakly corroborating a seam before the register header proper begins at Neh.7.6.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting v.5 itself between the security material and a register preface fails outright (rows cannot split mid-verse), and even reading it whole as the register's own opening loses to keeping it with the frame, since the golah header's own demonstrative opener does not appear until Neh.7.6.

boundary_rationale: "אֵ֣לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י הַמְּדִינָ֗ה הָעֹלִים֙" (web:Neh.7.6, “These are the children of the province who went up out of the captivity...”) is the book's single verbatim occurrence of this exact demonstrative-header phrase (sweep: 1 book-wide for eleh benei ha-medinah), one instance within a broader 7-member class of verse-initial eleh/ve'eleh demonstrative headers (MT 7.6, 7.61, 7.64, 11.3, 11.7, 12.1, 12.26) (device inventory: golah-register header), typologically matching Ezra 2.1 as a recension pair (cross-book metadata alone, not boundary authority). Neh.7.7 names the co-returning leaders and then supplies the formula that governs every numbered entry to come, "מִסְפַּ֕ר אַנְשֵׁ֖י עַ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵֽל" (web:Neh.7.7, “The number of the men of the people of Israel:”). MT 7:7 opens with the participle הַבָּאִ֣ים ('who came'), continuing 7:6's own relative chain as one unbroken sentence, with no mark of any kind between the two verses in pmarks_Neh.json -- an unmarked, grammatically continuous seam that rules out splitting the header (7:6) from the heading formula (7:7) as a considered alternative in its own right. A samekh follows Neh.7.7 (single-witness) -- weak corroboration, but it sits exactly where the heading formula hands off to the opening counted clan at Neh.7.8, supporting this unit as header-plus-heading rather than the start of the itemized count. Ch.7 overall carries 45 marks (5 petuchah + 40 samekh, all single-witness, re-derived directly from pmarks_Neh.json and matching strategy sec.4 exactly) at entry-level density through this register; that density is disclosed here once rather than re-argued at every seam below.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding Neh.7.6-7 into the opening numbered entry (Neh.7.8ff) as one register-opening row loses because מִסְפַּ֕ר אַנְשֵׁ֖י עַ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵֽל is a verbless construct-chain rubric carrying no numeral of its own, unlike every entry from Neh.7.8 on, which pairs a clan or town name with a figure.

boundary_rationale: The class begins at its initial counted entry, "בְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔שׁ" (web:Neh.7.8, “The children of Parosh: two thousand one hundred seventy-two.”), directly answering Neh.7.7's heading formula, and runs through entries using both the benei and anshei formula heads alike -- the two are interchangeable entry formulas rather than a clan-versus-town taxonomy, since benei itself governs place names three times within this span (“בְּנֵ֥י גִבְע֖וֹן”, Gibeon, oshb:Neh.7.25; “בְּנֵ֣י יְרֵח֔וֹ”, Jericho, oshb:Neh.7.36; “בְּנֵי לֹד֙ חָדִ֣יד”, Lod/Hadid/Ono, oshb:Neh.7.37) -- and the formula alternation (town-headed entries Neh.7.26-Neh.7.33 sit between clan-phrased entries on both sides, resuming at Neh.7.34) tracks no consistent semantic distinction and marks no fresh class, so it is texture within one list, not a seam. The class closes at "בְּנֵ֣י סְנָאָ֔ה" (web:Neh.7.38, “The children of Senaah: three thousand nine hundred thirty.”), immediately before the next unit opens with its own resumptive class name, "הַֽכֹּהֲנִ֑ים" (web:Neh.7.39, “The priests: The children of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua:...”), the same construction later repeated for Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants. No mark is invoked as evidence for this row; the class-header contrast alone carries the boundary on both edges.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Subdividing at Neh.7.26 where town-name entries begin loses under the standing rule against segmenting registers at bare connective or formulaic alternation rather than at an actual class header.

boundary_rationale: Opens on the resumptive class name "הַֽכֹּהֲנִ֑ים" (web:Neh.7.39, “The priests: The children of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua:...”), paralleling Neh.7.43's "הַלְוִיִּ֑ם" and the other class heads later in the same register -- a real taxonomic marker, not mere continuation of the laity list. Entries run Jedaiah, Immer, Pashhur, and close at "בְּנֵ֣י חָרִ֔ם" (web:Neh.7.42, “The children of Harim: one thousand seventeen.”), immediately before "הַלְוִיִּ֑ם" opens the next class at Neh.7.43. A petuchah follows oshb:Neh.7.38 (single-witness) at the front seam, samekh follows Neh.7.39, Neh.7.40, and Neh.7.41 (single-witness, three consecutive), and a second petuchah follows Neh.7.42 (single-witness) at the rear seam -- full symmetry disclosed for this narrow span.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading Neh.7.39-42 as a mere continuation of the laity count (one long returnee-count row from Neh.7.8) loses because the class-name construction is the same device that demonstrably reopens at every later subgroup in this register.

boundary_rationale: Three sub-classes share this row: Levites "הַלְוִיִּ֑ם" (web:Neh.7.43, “The Levites: the children of Jeshua, of Kadmiel, of the children of Hodevah:...”), singers "הַֽמְשֹׁרְרִ֑ים" (web:Neh.7.44, “The singers: the children of Asaph: one hundred forty-eight.”), and gatekeepers "הַשֹּֽׁעֲרִ֗ים" (web:Neh.7.45, “The gatekeepers: the children of Shallum, the children of Ater, the children of Talmon, the children of Akkub, the children of Hatita, the children of Shobai:...”). Each opens with its own class name, and the register's own device would license three separate rows on that naming alone, as it does elsewhere in this list; what binds these three together instead is an appointment made five verses before the register opens: “וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר נִבְנְתָה֙ הַחוֹמָ֔ה וָאַעֲמִ֖יד הַדְּלָת֑וֹת וַיִּפָּֽקְד֛וּ הַשּׁוֹעֲרִ֥ים וְהַמְשֹׁרְרִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּֽם” (oshb:Neh.7.1, gloss: 'and the gatekeepers and the singers and the Levites were appointed'), which names exactly these three temple offices as one administratively constituted set. That appointment, not the marks, is this row's grouping warrant; the marks are disclosed only as corroboration, tier-3 and non-driving in either direction. The triad is bracketed by the priests before and the temple servants ("הַנְּתִינִ֑ים", web:Neh.7.46, “The temple servants: the children of Ziha, the children of Hasupha, the children of Tabbaoth,”) after. A petuchah follows Neh.7.42 (single-witness) at the front seam and samekh follows Neh.7.43, Neh.7.44, and Neh.7.45 (single-witness) throughout the interior.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting Levites, singers, and gatekeepers into three separate rows is the register's default class-header practice everywhere else in ch.7, but it loses here because MT 7:1's appointment clause already names these three offices as one administratively constituted set, a textual warrant absent from the register's other class-name boundaries, which rest on naming alone (the priestly close at 7:42, the laity formula above, the joint total closing at 7:60).

boundary_rationale: Opens on "הַנְּתִינִ֑ים" (web:Neh.7.46, “The temple servants: the children of Ziha, the children of Hasupha, the children of Tabbaoth,”), the temple-servant (nethinim) class, runs eleven unmarked entries, then a second class name, "בְּנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה" (web:Neh.7.57, “The children of Solomon's servants: the children of Sotai, the children of Sophereth, the children of Perida,...”), introduces Solomon's-servants entries. The two classes are nonetheless one accounting unit: the closing verse totals them jointly, "כָּל הַ֨נְּתִינִ֔ים וּבְנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה" (web:Neh.7.60, “All the temple servants and the children of Solomon's servants were three hundred ninety-two.”), which is direct proof the author counted them together rather than as separately tallied classes. A samekh follows Neh.7.45 (single-witness) at the front seam and a petuchah follows Neh.7.60 (single-witness) at the rear, before "וְאֵ֗לֶּה הָֽעוֹלִים֙" opens the undocumented appendix at Neh.7.61.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting temple servants (Neh.7.46-56) from Solomon's servants (Neh.7.57-60) at the class-name change loses because the combined summary figure at Neh.7.60 shows the two classes were tallied as a single unit, not two.

boundary_rationale: A fresh reference opens the unit, “וְאֵ֗לֶּה הָֽעוֹלִים֙” (web:Neh.7.61, “These were those who went up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer; but they could not show their fathers’ houses, nor their offspring, whether they were of Israel:”), naming lay households unable to prove Israelite descent. The unit closes on their bare numeral tally, “The children of Delaiah, the children of Tobiah, the children of Nekoda: six hundred forty-two.” (web:Neh.7.62), with no verdict attached to the count. A petuchah follows Neh.7.60 (single-witness) at the front seam and a samekh follows Neh.7.62 (single-witness) at the rear, ahead of the priestly case that opens at Neh.7.63, “וּמִן הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים” — grammatically a continuation of the ve’elleh-ha’olim frame (waw-conjoined, unlike this register’s other class heads, which open asyndetically), but a shift to a different class of claimants whose case receives its own verdict at 7:64-65 rather than a bare tally.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping Neh.7.61-65 together as one undocumented-lineage row is the genuine rival: 7:63’s waw-conjoined u-min-hakkohanim opener continues, rather than restarts, the ve’elleh-ha’olim frame (this register’s other class heads — 7:39, 7:43, 7:44, 7:45, 7:46, 7:57 — all open asyndetically; sweep: the exact partitive-plus-noun string is 1 book-wide, the bare u-min 5 book-wide with 7:63 alone clause-initial in ch.7), so a fresh-class-head argument from syntax does not carry this seam. What still distinguishes 7:61-62 from what follows is outcome: the lay tally at 7:62 closes with a bare number and no stated disposition, while the priestly case beginning at 7:63 is explicitly adjudicated (disqualification at 7:64, the Tirshatha’s ruling at 7:65) — a different kind of unit than a headcount.

boundary_rationale: "וּמִן הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים" (web:Neh.7.63, “Of the priests: the children of Hobaiah, the children of Hakkoz, the children of Barzillai,...”) reopens the undocumented-lineage problem for three priestly houses; Neh.7.64 records their disqualification, and the Tirshatha's ruling follows with vav-consecutive continuity, "וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַתִּרְשָׁ֨תָא֙" (web:Neh.7.65, “The governor told them not to eat of the most holy things until a priest stood up to minister with Urim and Thummim.”), making Neh.7.63-65 one causal chain (claim, verdict, remedy) rather than three loosely joined notices. The chain ends before the register shifts register-level entirely to an aggregate formula, "כָּל הַקָּהָ֖ל כְּאֶחָ֑ד" (Neh.7.66), summing the whole assembly rather than one more family.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The genuine rival is backward, not forward: merging with Neh.7.61-62 into one undocumented-lineage row. Neh.7.63’s waw-conjoined opener continues rather than restarts the register’s resumptive frame, and 7:64’s own anaphoric demonstrative, “אֵ֗לֶּה בִּקְשׁ֧וּ כְתָבָ֛ם” (“these searched for their genealogical records”), reaches back to the same failed-proof standard already applied to the lay households at 7:61 — real continuity across the seam. What still holds 7:63-65 apart as its own unit is outcome: a stated disqualification (7:64) and the Tirshatha’s formal ruling barring the most holy things until Urim and Thummim are restored (7:65), a causal claim-verdict-remedy chain bound by vav-consecutive continuity that the bare lay tally at 7:62 never receives. Extending forward into the aggregate at Neh.7.66 remains the weaker rival: kol-hakkahal-ke’echad operates at a different level of the text, a whole-assembly count, not another itemized case.

boundary_rationale: "כָּל הַקָּהָ֖ל כְּאֶחָ֑ד" (web:Neh.7.66, “The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,”) opens an aggregate-total unit distinct in kind from every entry before it: whole-assembly headcount (Neh.7.66), servants and singers (web:Neh.7.67, “in addition to their male servants and their female servants, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven. They had two hundred forty-five singing men and singing women.”), then livestock. web:Neh.7.68, “Their horses were seven hundred thirty-six; their mules, two hundred forty-five;”, has NO WLC counterpart -- the Hebrew behind oshb runs directly from the servant/singer total (oshb:Neh.7.67) to the camels figure (oshb:Neh.7.68, aliased web:Neh.7.69, "גְּמַלִּ֕ים..."); no oshb ref or mark claim is made for WEB 7:68 and its original-language status is insufficient_evidence in WLC. The variant is paralleled by Ezra 2.66, which does carry a horses-and-mules line (cross-book metadata alone, not boundary authority; figures are not harmonized between the two witnesses of this recension). Samekh follows oshb:Neh.7.67 (single-witness) and a second samekh follows oshb:Neh.7.68 (single-witness) (WEB 7:69), closing this totals unit right before the treasury gifts open at Neh.7.70.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating Neh.7.66-73 as one undifferentiated totals-and-colophon row, closer to the strategy's own coarser block-map wording, loses because a real grammatical subject-shift opens a distinct treasury-donations unit at Neh.7.70, and the 7:68 zone variant deserves its own disclosed seam rather than burial inside an eight-verse span.

boundary_rationale: A new grammatical subject opens this unit, "וּמִקְצָת֙ רָאשֵׁ֣י הָֽאָב֔וֹת" (web:Neh.7.70, “Some from among the heads of fathers' households gave to the work. The governor gave to the treasury one thousand darics of gold, fifty basins, and five hundred thirty priests' garments.”), shifting the register from population and livestock counts to itemized darics, basins, and garments given toward the work -- beginning with the governor, then household heads, then "וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתְנוּ֮ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית הָעָם֒" (web:Neh.7.72, “That which the rest of the people gave was twenty thousand darics of gold, plus two thousand minas of silver, and sixty-seven priests' garments.”). Samekh follows oshb:Neh.7.68 (single-witness) (WEB 7:69) at the front seam, and a petuchah follows oshb:Neh.7.71 (single-witness) (WEB 7:72) at the rear, immediately before the register drops the itemized-gift idiom and the narrative resumes in summary mode at Neh.7.73.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through the colophon (Neh.7.70-73) loses because Neh.7.73 resumes narrative-summary mode (vayeshevu) rather than continuing the darics-and-garments accounting, and the single-witness petuchah after oshb:Neh.7.71 corroborates a seam right there.

boundary_rationale: The register closes in summary-narrative mode, "וַיֵּשְׁב֣וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֡ם וְהַשּׁוֹעֲרִים֩ וְהַמְשֹׁרְרִ֨ים וּמִן הָעָ֧ם וְהַנְּתִינִ֛ים וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּעָרֵיהֶ֑ם" (web:Neh.7.73, “So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel lived in their cities.”), listing the same classes named at Neh.7.39, Neh.7.43, Neh.7.44, Neh.7.45, and Neh.7.46 (priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants) now as settled residents rather than counted entries -- a clean close to the golah-register unit that this part has been arguing since Neh.7.6. The verse then adds a second clause, "וַיִּגַּע֙ הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י וּבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּעָרֵיהֶֽם" (web:Neh.7.73, “When the seventh month had come, the children of Israel were in their cities.”), whose force is genuinely double-sided: it can read as this colophon's own dating notice, or as the temporal frame that Neh.8.1's assembly account (outside this part) opens into. Neh.7.72 through Neh.8.1 (MT) runs parallel to Ezra 2.70-3.1, where the settlement-and-seventh-month notice likewise sits directly against the gathering that follows (cross-book metadata alone; the recension continues through this hinge in both witnesses without settling which side of the seam owns the clause). This part's claim is limited to "וַיִּגַּע֙ הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י וּבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּעָרֵיהֶֽם" belonging with the colophon it stands in; it does not claim Neh.8.1 or resolve the live question of whether the seventh-month clause also functions as that chapter's opening frame.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading the seventh-month clause as already opening 8:1’s assembly (one row spanning the seam) loses on textual grounds: 7:73b’s own wayyiqtol, וַיִּגַּע֙ הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י, is immediately closed by its own resumptive, וּבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּעָרֵיהֶֽם, repeating the settlement statement and keeping the clause syntactically inside the colophon rather than opening forward the way Neh.8.1’s own vayye’asfu opens its own scene — though this resolves the syntax alone, not whether the same clause also frames 8:1 from the far side of the seam.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a fresh collective wayyiqtol with a new-subject convocation formula, “וַיֵּאָסְפ֤וּ כָל הָעָם֙ כְּאִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֔ד” (web:Neh.8.1 “All the people gathered themselves together as one man”), naming a specific locale (the wide place before the Water Gate) and a specific request (bring the book of Moses’ law) that is absent from the preceding golah-register colophon. That colophon (web:Neh.7.73) closes instead on a settlement notice and its own month-arrival clause bracketed by a resumptive, “וַיִּגַּע֙ הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י וּבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּעָרֵיהֶֽם” (oshb:Neh.7.72 (WEB 7:73) “When the seventh month had come, the children of Israel were in their cities.”) — a chronological hinge, not an assembly-convening act. The cross-book recension parallel (Ezra chapter 2 verse 70 through chapter 3 verse 1) carries the settlement notice directly into a gathering at Jerusalem; per campaign rule this is typed-relation metadata only and never harmonized into Neh’s own wording. The live question this leaves open at the part seam: whether 7:73b’s month-arrival clause functions as a shared temporal frame that keeps 7:73 and 8:1 as one continuous unit (as the Ezra parallel might suggest), or whether 8:1’s fresh-subject wayyiqtol convocation is sufficient on its own to open a fresh unit regardless of how 7:73’s internal seam is resolved on the adjoining part. From this side, the three-part gathering formula vayye’asfu kol ha’am ke’ish echad is a book-wide singleton (sweep: 1, Neh.8.1 only); the niphal wayyiqtol vayye’asfu recurs at 12:28 (sweep: 2 book-wide), where the subject shifts to benei ha-meshor’rim, and the niphal qatal ne’esfu recurs at 8:13 and 9:1 (sweep: 2 book-wide), giving 4 ASF-root gatherings across the book. A singleton formula cannot by itself establish a recurring device, so this boundary rests on the subject, locale, and request shift argued above, not on recurrence. The unit runs through the initial public reading and closes on the attentiveness notice at 8:3, “וְאָזְנֵ֥י כָל הָעָ֖ם אֶל סֵ֥פֶר הַתּוֹרָֽה” (web:Neh.8.3 “The ears of all the people were attentive to the book of the law”), before the platform staging of 8:4 introduces named assistants.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 7:73 and 8:1 as one continuous recension-driven unit is the strongest rival, but it would require importing an Ezra-side boundary into Neh’s own text rather than arguing from Neh’s own new-subject wayyiqtol convocation, locale, and request shift, which this part’s brief reserves as a live cross-part question rather than a settled merge.

boundary_rationale: A fresh spatial staging opens the scene, “וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֞ד עֶזְרָ֣א הַסֹּפֵ֗ר עַֽל מִגְדַּל עֵץ֮” (web:Neh.8.4 “Ezra the scribe stood on a pulpit of wood”), immediately followed by a named right-hand/left-hand assistant list absent from the mass-subject kol ha’am framing of the initial gathering. A petuchah (PE, single-witness) follows Neh.8.4 itself, falling between 8:4 and 8:5 — interior to this row, one verse in from its own opening seam, which carries no mark of its own — and is overridden here by the tier-1 staging and participant-shift argument rather than treated as corroboration for that opening seam. The unit closes on the reading-technique summary, the whole of 8:8, “וַֽיִּקְרְא֥וּ בַסֵּ֛פֶר בְּתוֹרַ֥ת הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים מְפֹרָ֑שׁ וְשׂ֣וֹם שֶׂ֔כֶל וַיָּבִ֖ינוּ בַּמִּקְרָֽא” (web:Neh.8.8 “They read in the book, in the law of God, distinctly… so that they understood the reading”), after which a setumah (SAMEKH, single-witness) follows — disclosed here alongside the interior petuchah to satisfy full front/interior/end symmetry for this span. The reading-technique description ends before the leaders’ own direct speech begins in the verse that follows.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through the leaders’ celebratory instructions would merge the reading-technique description with their emotional-reframing speech act, collapsing a description-to-direct-discourse pivot that this row’s own closing mark weakly corroborates.

boundary_rationale: Direct discourse opens the unit, “וַיֹּ֣אמֶר נְחֶמְיָ֣ה ה֣וּא הַתִּרְשָׁ֡תָא וְעֶזְרָ֣א הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַסֹּפֵ֡ר וְהַלְוִיִּם֩ הַמְּבִינִ֨ים אֶת הָעָ֜ם” (web:Neh.8.9 “Nehemiah, who was the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who taught the people said…”), pivoting from the reading-technique report of 8:4-8 into named-leader speech; its declarative core, “הַיּ֤וֹם קָדֹֽשׁ הוּא֙ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם” (“Today is holy to Yahweh your God”), is echoed at 8:10-11 and frames the whole exchange. The unit closes on the people’s compliance and its stated cause, “כִּ֤י הֵבִ֨ינוּ֙ בַּדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹדִ֖יעוּ לָהֶֽם” (web:Neh.8.12 “because they had understood the words that were declared to them”), after which a setumah (SAMEKH, single-witness) follows — tier-3 corroboration only, disclosed here for front/interior/end symmetry with the adjoining span — before the second-day frame of 8:13, “וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשֵּׁנִ֡י” (web:Neh.8.13, “On the second day”), reopens the scene at a new date.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting 8:9-10 (the leaders’ speech) from 8:11-12 (the Levites’ echo and the people’s response) treats one continuous speech-and-compliance exchange as two units without any tier-1 frame break between them.
