boundary_rationale: A fresh temporal marker reopens the scene, “וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשֵּׁנִ֡י נֶאֶסְפוּ֩ רָאשֵׁ֨י הָאָב֜וֹת” (web:Neh.8.13 “On the second day, the heads of fathers’ households… were gathered together”), introducing a study session distinct from the opening-day reading and celebration of 8:1-12. The rediscovery formula, “וַֽיִּמְצְא֖וּ כָּת֣וּב בַּתּוֹרָ֑ה” (web:Neh.8.14 “They found written in the law”), leads into the Sukkot command, “יֵשְׁב֨וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל בַּסֻּכּ֛וֹת בֶּחָ֖ג בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי” (“the children of Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month”). The unit closes on the fulfillment summary, “וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ חָג֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים וּבַיּ֧וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֛י עֲצֶ֖רֶת כַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט” (web:Neh.8.18 “They kept the feast seven days; and on the eighth day was a solemn assembly, according to the ordinance”), a formal completion notice before 9:1 opens an entirely new dated assembly. Cross-book note: the ch.8 reading-and-festival account parallels 1 Esdras chapter 9’s assembly narrative; typed-relation metadata only, not used to argue this boundary.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit to include 9:1 would conflate a completed, formulaically closed festival notice with a new dated fast-assembly that opens under a different (penitential, sackcloth-and-dirt) register.

boundary_rationale: A dated notice opens the unit, “וּבְיוֹם֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֜ה לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֗ה נֶאֶסְפ֤וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּצ֣וֹם וּבְשַׂקִּ֔ים וַאֲדָמָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶֽם” (web:Neh.9.1 “in the twenty-fourth day of this month the children of Israel were assembled with fasting, with sackcloth, and dirt on them”), sharply distinct in register from ch.8’s festal close, “וַתְּהִ֥י שִׂמְחָ֖ה גְּדוֹלָ֥ה מְאֹֽד” (web:Neh.8.17 “There was very great gladness”) — sackcloth and dirt against booths and gladness. The separation and posture that mark this a fast-assembly continue through the frame, “וַיִּבָּֽדְלוּ֙ זֶ֣רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִכֹּ֖ל בְּנֵ֣י נֵכָ֑ר” (web:Neh.9.2 “The offspring of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners”) and “וַיָּק֨וּמוּ֙ עַל עָמְדָ֔ם” (web:Neh.9.3 “They stood up in their place”). A petuchah (PE, single-witness) follows 8:18, edge-adjacent to this row’s own opening seam; a second petuchah follows 9:3, interior to this row (falling between 9:3 and 9:4) and, as tier-3 corroboration, pulling weakly toward a 9:1-3 close that this row declines on tier-1 grounds: 9:4 itself opens with the same singular-standing-verb-plus-elevated-locus-plus-named-list configuration that marks the platform staging at 8:4 — “וַיָּ֜קָם עַֽל מַֽעֲלֵ֣ה הַלְוִיִּ֗ם יֵשׁ֨וּעַ וּבָנִ֜י קַדְמִיאֵ֧ל…” (web:Neh.9.4) against “וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֞ד עֶזְרָ֣א הַסֹּפֵ֗ר עַֽל מִגְדַּל עֵץ֮” (web:Neh.8.4) — yet the list at 9:4 partly reprises the Levite leadership already named at 8:7 (Yeshua, Bani, Sherebyah, and Hodiyah recur across both lists) rather than introducing an unfamiliar cast to stage a wholly new scene, so what actually holds 9:4 inside this unit is discourse mode, not the list itself: the verse still reports the crying-aloud in narrated summary, “וַיָּ֜קָם עַֽל מַֽעֲלֵ֣ה הַלְוִיִּ֗ם יֵשׁ֨וּעַ וּבָנִ֜י קַדְמִיאֵ֧ל שְׁבַנְיָ֛ה בֻּנִּ֥י שֵׁרֵבְיָ֖ה בָּנִ֣י כְנָ֑נִי וַֽיִּזְעֲקוּ֙ בְּק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל אֶל יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם” (web:Neh.9.4 “cried with a loud voice to Yahweh their God”), rather than in the direct-speech quotation that only begins at 9:5. Both marks are disclosed as weak corroboration only, never a driver.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The genuine rival is extending this frame to include the whole of 9:5 rather than closing at 9:4; it fails because 9:5 opens with its own direct-speech marker, “וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ הַלְוִיִּ֡ם” (“then the Levites said”), pivoting from this row’s narrated crying-aloud into the prayer’s own verbatim doxological summons, so 9:4 is this row’s true final verse.

boundary_rationale: The imperative summons, “ק֗וּמוּ בָּרֲכוּ֙ אֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם מִן הָעוֹלָ֖ם עַד הָעוֹלָ֑ם” (web:Neh.9.5 “Stand up and bless Yahweh your God from everlasting to everlasting”), is a direct-address command distinct in mood from both the narrated crying-aloud of 9:4 and the second-person declarative recital that opens at 9:6; it functions as the prayer’s doxological threshold. Its close, “וִיבָֽרְכוּ֙ שֵׁ֣ם כְּבוֹדֶ֔ךָ וּמְרוֹמַ֥ם עַל כָּל בְּרָכָ֖ה וּתְהִלָּֽה” (“Blessed be your glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise”), invokes the name before the recital’s own "you are" clauses begin. Because the whole verse contains both the minimal speech-attribution clause and the summons itself, and rows may not split mid-verse, the whole verse is assigned here rather than to 9:1-4 because the frame travels with its inset; a forward merger with 9:6 is the weaker contest by comparison, since 9:6 opens its own declarative “atah hu” recital move in a mood distinct from 9:5’s imperative summons. As part of the prayer spanning 9:5b-37, this verse supplies its doxological opening threshold, immediately before the creation epoch opens at 9:6.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 9:5 to the 9:1-4 assembly frame ignores the direct-speech pivot ("said," introducing verbatim discourse) that switches from narrated summary into the prayer’s own opening doxology.

boundary_rationale: The recital proper opens with a declarative self-naming, “אַתָּה ה֣וּא יְהוָה֮ לְבַדֶּךָ֒” (web:Neh.9.6 “You are Yahweh, even you alone”), syntactically distinct from the imperative summons of 9:5. Its content turns to cosmology, “אַתָּ֣ה עָשִׂ֡יתָ אֶֽת הַשָּׁמַיִם֩ שְׁמֵ֨י הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם וְכָל צְבָאָ֗ם” (“You have made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their army”), matching the creation epoch strategy identifies at this verse. MT 9:6 carries a catalogued ketiv/qere pair at this point: the unpointed ketiv “את” is traditionally read per the pointed qere “אַתָּ֣ה”, repeating the pronoun; the verb phrase quoted above follows the qere. This "atah hu" declarative recurs, with renewed subject-matter, at 9:7 (sweep: 2 book-wide, skeleton tier, Neh.9.6 and Neh.9.7), marking the device as the recital’s own internal epoch-marker rather than incidental repetition. The verse closes before 9:7 reopens the same formula to pivot into the Abraham material. Within the 9:5b-37 prayer, this verse opens the recital's creation epoch.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 9:6 into a combined 9:6-8 "patriarchal preface" row would blur the recital’s own repeated "atah hu" epoch-marker, which strategy treats as two distinct recital moments (creation; Abraham).

boundary_rationale: The recurrence of the divine self-naming, “אַתָּה הוּא֙ יְהוָ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּחַ֨רְתָּ֙ בְּאַבְרָ֔ם” (web:Neh.9.7 “You are Yahweh, the God who chose Abram”), marks this epoch’s opening, narrowing from cosmic creation to the particular election and renaming of Abraham and the land-covenant given him. The epoch closes on a covenant-fidelity verdict, “וַתָּ֨קֶם֙ אֶת דְּבָרֶ֔יךָ כִּ֥י צַדִּ֖יק אָֽתָּה” (web:Neh.9.8 “have performed your words, for you are righteous”), before 9:9’s shift to communal "our fathers" language opens the Egypt material. This unit occupies the 9:5b-37 prayer's Abraham/election epoch, continuing the atah-hu recital marker introduced at 9:6.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 9:7-8 into the creation row ignores the repeated "atah hu" recital-marker that separates the two epochs in strategy’s own reading.

boundary_rationale: A shift in referent marks the opening, “וַתֵּ֛רֶא אֶת עֳנִ֥י אֲבֹתֵ֖ינוּ בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם” (web:Neh.9.9 “You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt”), reframing the recital from divine-name declaratives about the patriarch into a 2ms recital whose 1cp possessive suffix (avoteinu, “our fathers”) aligns the praying community with the Egypt-era ancestors, opening the Exodus material. The epoch runs through the sea-crossing, “וְהַיָּם֙ בָּקַ֣עְתָּ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּֽעַבְר֥וּ בְתוֹךְ הַיָּ֖ם בַּיַּבָּשָׁ֑ה” (web:Neh.9.11 “You divided the sea before them, so that they went through the middle of the sea on the dry land”), and the drowning of the pursuers, closing where 9:12 shifts topic to the wilderness guidance-pillar material. Continuing the recital from the Abraham/election material at 9:7-8, this span forms the 9:5b-37 prayer's Egypt/sea epoch.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through 9:12 merges the sea-crossing narrative with the guidance-pillar motif; the seam is more than topical, since 9:9's fronted object זַעֲקָתָ֥ם and 9:11's fronted object וְהַיָּם֙ both front a direct object before their qatal verb, while 9:12's doubled וּבְעַמּ֣וּד עָנָ֔ן הִנְחִיתָ֖ם fronts a locative/instrumental phrase before its verb instead — a different fronting category that marks the guidance-pillar material as its own recital move.

boundary_rationale: This single-verse epoch, the whole of 9:12, “וּבְעַמּ֣וּד עָנָ֔ן הִנְחִיתָ֖ם יוֹמָ֑ם וּבְעַמּ֥וּד אֵשׁ֙ לַ֔יְלָה לְהָאִ֣יר לָהֶ֔ם אֶת הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵֽלְכוּ בָֽהּ” (web:Neh.9.12 “in a pillar of cloud you led them by day; and in a pillar of fire by night, to give them light in the way in which they should go”), shifts topic from the sea-crossing and drowned pursuers to the wilderness guidance-pillar, the recital move §6 assigns this verse on its own; the construction opening it, conjunctive waw plus a fronted adverbial before a 2ms qatal, is shared across 9:11-9:15 and so does not itself mark the seam. It closes before 9:13’s shift in topic and locale (“on Mount Sinai”) opens the lawgiving epoch. The same pillar-of-cloud/fire imagery recurs almost verbatim at 9:19, where strategy reads it as a separate “sustaining mercy” epoch reprising the motif under a forgiveness frame rather than as evidence for merging the two passages. Set between the Egypt/sea and Sinai epochs, this verse is the 9:5b-37 prayer's wilderness-guidance moment.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 9:12 into the following Sinai epoch (9:13-14) ignores the shift in topic and locale (“on Mount Sinai”) that strategy marks as its own recital moment.

boundary_rationale: A shift in topic to lawgiving opens this epoch at Neh.9.13, “וְעַ֤ל הַר סִינַי֙ יָרַ֔דְתָּ” (web:Neh.9.13 “You also came down on Mount Sinai”), covering ordinances, statutes, and Sabbath — the recital move §6 assigns this verse, distinct in content from the guidance-pillar material before it though sharing its conjunctive-waw-plus-fronted-constituent shape. The epoch closes on the transmission formula naming its mediator, “בְּיַ֖ד מֹשֶׁ֥ה עַבְדֶּֽךָ” (web:Neh.9.14 “by Moses your servant”), before 9:15 opens the wilderness-provision material with its own fresh topic (bread and water). The 9:5b-37 prayer counts this as its Sinai/lawgiving epoch, closing the middle recital sequence before the plea proper begins.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 9:13-14 with 9:15 blurs Sinai’s revelation-content (ordinances, sabbath, law) with the distinct provision narrative that strategy separates as its own recital moment.

boundary_rationale: This single-verse epoch opens on a fresh topic-initial clause, “וְ֠לֶחֶם מִשָּׁמַ֜יִם נָתַ֤תָּה לָהֶם֙ לִרְעָבָ֔ם” (web:Neh.9.15 “gave them bread from the sky for their hunger”), continuing the same 2ms qatal address-forms as 9:13-14 (yaradta, hoda'ta, tzivita) with vav attached to each fronted topical constituent rather than to the verb itself — not a weqatal chain. What discriminates this verse from its Sinai-lawgiving predecessor is content-category (provision rather than statute), since the syntax itself supplies no break across the 9:14/15 seam. The verse closes on the land-oath clause, “אֲשֶׁר נָשָׂ֥אתָ אֶת יָדְךָ֖ לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶֽם” (web:Neh.9.15 “which you had sworn to give them”), completing the pre-rebellion recital's double provision (bread and water paired with the promise of the land) before 9:16's adversative “וְהֵ֥ם וַאֲבֹתֵ֖ינוּ הֵזִ֑ידוּ” (web:Neh.9.16 “But they and our fathers behaved proudly”) turns the recital to apostasy. The water clause recurs almost verbatim at 9:20 (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, 9:15 and 9:20), but there it sits embedded inside the post-calf mercy epoch with no comparable oath clause or adversative pivot following it, so the repetition does not license a seam at 9:20 the way it does here. As part of the prayer spanning 9:5b-37, this verse supplies its provision epoch, within the pre-rebellion recital.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The genuinely adjacent rival is a backward merge into 9:13-14: the 2ms qatal address-chain (yaradta, hoda'ta, tzivita, natata, hotzeta) runs uninterrupted across the 9:14/15 seam, with vav attached to each fronted constituent rather than the verb, and no adversative or vocative-reset marker distinguishes 9:15 syntactically from its neighbors. It still loses because the split from Sinai's lawgiving rests on content-category (statute versus provision) rather than any syntactic break — the kind of seam strategy draws at recital-topic shifts, not clause-chain breaks — while the far weaker forward-merge into 9:19-21 is defeated outright by the intervening rebellion and golden-calf material of 9:16-18.

boundary_rationale: The adversative opener, “וְהֵ֥ם וַאֲבֹתֵ֖ינוּ הֵזִ֑ידוּ” (web:Neh.9.16 “But they and our fathers behaved proudly”), marks the recital's pivot into rebellion, opposing the preceding provision material with a hardened-neck refusal. The unit's own interior already turns briefly toward forgiveness at 9:17b, “וְאַתָּה֩ אֱל֨וֹהַּ סְלִיח֜וֹת ... וְלֹ֥א עֲזַבְתָּֽם” (web:Neh.9.17 “But you are a God ready to pardon ... and didn’t forsake them”) — the same waw-plus-independent-pronoun divine predicate closing on the identical negated verb that anchors 9:19's opener (the vav-plus-pronoun opener itself recurs at 9:17 and 9:19 only, sweep: 2 book-wide in this construction; the bare negated verb azavtam recurs in a third verse, 9:31, sweep: 3 book-wide, though there אָֽתָּה stands verse-final and non-vav-prefixed, in a different clause from 9:17/9:19's opener); here, though, it sits embedded within the sequence of refusals as a brief aside subordinate to the rebellion narrative, not yet answering it the way 9:19's fuller, fronted restatement does. The epoch's low point opens with the concessive “אַ֗ף כִּֽי עָשׂ֤וּ לָהֶם֙ עֵ֣גֶל מַסֵּכָ֔ה” (web:Neh.9.18 “Yes, when they had made themselves a molded calf”), and the verse's own close, not this mid-verse clause, supplies the epoch's boundary: “וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ נֶאָצ֖וֹת גְּדֹלֽוֹת” (web:Neh.9.18 “and had committed awful blasphemies”), a clause reprised almost verbatim — differing only in the adjective's plene spelling — at the close of 9:26, “וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ נֶאָצ֖וֹת גְּדוֹלֹֽת” (web:Neh.9.26 “and they committed awful blasphemies”; sweep: 2 verses book-wide), which is exactly what explains the thematic pull toward reading 9:26 as folding back into the golden-calf epoch — a reading the epoch that follows (9:26-9:28) treats as thematically motivated but spatially unavailable, not a live structural rival — before 9:19's own “yet you in your manifold mercies” reopens the recital with a forgiveness-focused adversative of its own. Within the 9:5b-37 prayer, this span forms the rebellion-and-golden-calf epoch.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing this unit at 9:17 (before the calf episode) severs the hardened-neck motif from its narrative climax: 9:16's rebellion pivot and 9:18's golden-calf blasphemy read here as one continuous sequence, not two.

boundary_rationale: The adversative-mercy opener, “וְאַתָּה֙ בְּרַחֲמֶ֣יךָ הָֽרַבִּ֔ים לֹ֥א עֲזַבְתָּ֖ם בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר” (web:Neh.9.19 “yet you in your manifold mercies didn’t forsake them in the wilderness”), directly answers the rebellion epoch and reprises the pillar-of-cloud/fire imagery of 9:12 under a forgiveness frame. It closes on the sustenance summary, “וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֛ה כִּלְכַּלְתָּ֥ם” (web:Neh.9.21 “forty years you sustained them”), before 9:22’s "moreover you gave them kingdoms" opens the conquest epoch with a fresh topic of territorial gift. This unit occupies the 9:5b-37 prayer's sustaining-mercy epoch, answering the rebellion just narrated.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit to 9:22 would merge the wilderness-sustenance summary with the conquest narrative's distinct topic (kingdoms and peoples) that strategy separates as its own recital moment.

boundary_rationale: The gift-formula opener, “וַתִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֤ם מַמְלָכוֹת֙ וַעֲמָמִ֔ים” (web:Neh.9.22 “you gave them kingdoms and peoples”), begins the territorial epoch, continuing across 9:22-23’s benefaction language before narrating the conquest itself (9:24) and its abundance (9:25). The epoch closes on a satiety formula, “וַיֹּאכְל֤וּ וַֽיִּשְׂבְּעוּ֙ וַיַּשְׁמִ֔ינוּ וַיִּֽתְעַדְּנ֖וּ בְּטוּבְךָ֥ הַגָּדֽוֹל” (web:Neh.9.25 “So they ate, were filled, became fat, and delighted themselves in your great goodness”), before 9:26’s adversative disobedience-and-rebellion opener reopens with the recital’s second rebellion turn. Within the 9:5b-37 prayer, this span forms the conquest-and-inheritance epoch.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting 9:22-23 (territorial gift, opening 2ms “וַתִּתֵּ֨ן”, “וּבְנֵיהֶ֣ם הִרְבִּ֔יתָ”) from 9:24-25 (conquest and abundance) over-atomizes what is a single recital moment: the agent alternates rather than breaks cleanly, with 9:22 already carrying a 3mp verb inside the 2ms frame (“וַיִּֽירְשׁ֞וּ”, "and they possessed"), 9:23 returning to 2ms, 9:24 opening with a re-nominalized 3mp subject (“וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ הַבָּנִים֙ וַיִּֽירְשׁ֣וּ”, "the children went in and possessed"), and 9:25 continuing 3mp; this alternation is unit texture running through the whole span, not a break isolating any one verse, so no split within 9:22-25 is warranted.

boundary_rationale: 9:25 closes on four unbroken 3mp wayyiqtols, “וַיֹּאכְל֤וּ וַֽיִּשְׂבְּעוּ֙ וַיַּשְׁמִ֔ינוּ וַיִּֽתְעַדְּנ֖וּ” (web:Neh.9.25 “So they ate, were filled, became fat, and delighted themselves”), and 9:26 continues the same chain with two more, “וַיַּמְר֨וּ וַֽיִּמְרְד֜וּ בָּ֗ךְ” (web:Neh.9.26 “they were disobedient and rebelled against you”) — form, person, and referent all carry across the seam, so no morphosyntactic break marks it. What does mark it is a satiety-to-apostasy inversion joined to a resumptive lexical bridge: 9:26 closes on “וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ נֶאָצ֖וֹת גְּדוֹלֹֽת” (web:Neh.9.26 “and they committed awful blasphemies”), echoing 9:18’s own close, “וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ נֶאָצ֖וֹת גְּדֹלֽוֹת” (web:Neh.9.18 “and had committed awful blasphemies”; sweep: 2 verses book-wide, the two differing only in the adjective's plene spelling), reopening the recital's cyclical oppression-deliverance pattern as a second rebellion turn. The cycle runs through 9:27's single distress-cry-deliverance sequence and 9:28's second, rest-relapse-oppression-cry-deliverance sequence, closing on the cycle’s own repetition marker, “וְאַתָּ֞ה מִשָּׁמַ֧יִם תִּשְׁמַ֛ע וְתַצִּילֵ֥ם כְּֽרַחֲמֶ֖יךָ רַבּ֥וֹת עִתִּֽים” (web:Neh.9.28 “you heard from heaven; and many times you delivered them according to your mercies”), before 9:29’s "and testified against them" opens the prophetic-witness epoch with its own testifying-verb topic. The 9:5b-37 prayer counts this as its judges-cycle epoch, reprising 9:16-18's apostasy under a new rebellion-and-deliverance pattern.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The genuinely adjacent rival is closing the cycle at 9:27 alone, before 9:28's second oppression-relapse-deliverance episode: it loses because 9:28’s generalizing close, “רַבּ֥וֹת עִתִּֽים” ("many times"), treats both episodes as one iterated cycle rather than two. Reading 9:26 as folding back into the golden-calf epoch (9:16-18) is not itself available as a segmentation option, since the recital moments already assigned between them intervene; the shared closing phrase ne'atzot gedolot/gedolot (9:18/9:26) explains the thematic pull toward that reading but marks classification kinship, not spatial adjacency.

boundary_rationale: The verb “וַתָּ֨עַד” ("and you testified") at 9:29 is 2ms — God himself is the subject, with the prophets appearing as instrument in the very next verse, “וַתָּ֨עַד בָּ֧ם בְּרוּחֲךָ֛ בְּיַד נְבִיאֶ֖יךָ” (web:Neh.9.30 “and testified against them by your Spirit through your prophets”). The testifying motif itself predates this seam — 9:26 already has “אֲשֶׁר הֵעִ֥ידוּ בָ֖ם” (web:Neh.9.26 “that testified against them”), 3mp, the prophets themselves as subject. The 2ms testify-form ta'ad recurs at 9:29 and 9:30 (sweep: 2 book-wide in this form; a third skeletal hit at 9:25 falls inside the unrelated word vayyit'adnu and is excluded), and the hifil testify-form he'id recurs at 9:26 and 9:34 (sweep: 2 book-wide, the second beyond this epoch's own span) — so what escalates here is not the motif but the agent: human intermediaries as testifiers at 9:26 give way to God's own direct, sustained testifying at 9:29-30, “לַהֲשִׁיבָ֣ם אֶל תּוֹרָתֶ֗ךָ” (web:Neh.9.29 “that you might bring them again to your law”). The epoch closes on “וּֽבְרַחֲמֶ֧יךָ הָרַבִּ֛ים לֹֽא עֲשִׂיתָ֥ם כָּלָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א עֲזַבְתָּ֑ם” (web:Neh.9.31 “Nevertheless in your manifold mercies you didn’t make a full end of them, nor forsake them”); rachamekha recurs in 4 verses book-wide (9:19, 9:27, 9:28, 9:31) and the negated azav in 3 (9:17, 9:19, 9:31), but the same collocation performs opposite roles a few verses apart — 9:31's instance stands in the epoch's own final verse and is answered immediately by the ve'atah pivot at 9:32, while 9:19's opens a verse that goes on to introduce fresh pillar-of-cloud content — so it legitimately closes this epoch and opened that one. As part of the prayer spanning 9:5b-37, this unit supplies its prophets-ignored epoch. Before 9:32’s "now therefore, our God" pivots the recital into the present-tense communal plea.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing this epoch at 9:30 (before the mercy refrain) severs 9:31's summarizing verdict from the epoch it concludes, leaving the refrain orphaned rather than read as this epoch's close, per strategy's own 9:29-31 grouping.

boundary_rationale: The pivot opener, “וְעַתָּ֣ה אֱ֠לֹהֵינוּ הָאֵ֨ל הַגָּד֜וֹל הַגִּבּ֣וֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא֮” (web:Neh.9.32 “Now therefore, our God, the great, the mighty, and the awesome God”), turns the recital from third-plural historical narration into a 1cp present-tense plea cataloguing communal suffering down through the closing clause of 9:37, “וּבְצָרָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה אֲנָֽחְנוּ” (web:Neh.9.37 “we are in great distress”), a state description that is syntactically closed. By contrast, 9:38 opens with an anaphoric prepositional phrase and a performative participle, “וּבְכָל זֹ֕את אֲנַ֛חְנוּ כֹּרְתִ֥ים אֲמָנָ֖ה וְכֹתְבִ֑ים” (oshb:Neh.10.1 (WEB 9:38) “Yet for all this, we make a sure covenant, and write it”) — a covenant-sealing speech act rather than a further plea-clause, whose connective "yet for all this" gathers up the preceding recital as grounds for the next act (sealing a document, continued in the ch.10 sealers list) rather than extending the plea. On this basis the prayer’s recital-and-plea unit is complete at 9:37, and 9:38 opens the covenant-sealing hinge argued from its own participial, address-free grammar. The nearest relevant mark is a petuchah (PE, single-witness) after 9:37 itself, corroborating a break at most weakly and never dispositive on its own. The live cross-part question, named without resolving it here: whether the plea of 9:32-37 and the covenant performative of 9:38 form one continuous rhetorical act (the plea implicitly demanding the remedy the covenant supplies) or two distinct units divided by the shift from descriptive complaint to legal performative. Parent grouping: sub-row of the great prayer 9:5b-37 (§6 policy), its closing present-distress epoch.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row to include 9:38 would blur the performative-shift and verbless-close distinction that most naturally opens a new textual act: 9:37 ends verblessly (u-vtzarah gedolah anachnu, "and we are in great distress"), while 9:38's clause carries just participles (koretim/kotvim) and no second-person address element at all, unlike every verse from 9:32 onward.

boundary_rationale: WEB "Yet for all this, we make a sure covenant, and write it; and our princes, our Levites, and our priests, seal it." The Hebrew opens with the resumptive “וּבְכָל זֹ֕את אֲנַ֛חְנוּ”, read here consecutively ("and in view of all this, we...") against the concessive value the WEB rendering above already supplies ("yet for all this"); the concessive sense is what ties the clause back to the distress just narrated, while the consecutive sense is what carries the pivot to the resolve that follows, and both readings are live. The pronoun itself, anachnu, continues the prayer's own 1cp chain rather than introducing a fresh one (sweep: 15 verses book-wide, four of them within the 9:33 through 9:38 span: 9:33, 9:36 twice, 9:37, and this verse) — a continuity that does not, by itself, make this verse a further petition clause: it contains no verb of address to God and no petition verb of the kind that runs through the plea preceding it, merely the resolve “כֹּרְתִ֥ים אֲמָנָ֖ה וְכֹתְבִ֑ים” ("cutting a firm covenant, and writing [it]") — a performative bicolon (cut, write), not a tricolon, since the verse's third element, “וְעַל֙ הֶֽחָת֔וּם שָׂרֵ֥ינוּ לְוִיֵּ֖נוּ כֹּהֲנֵֽינוּ” ("and upon the sealed [thing], our princes, our Levites, our priests"), is a verbless clause: hechatum is a definite passive participle governed by the preposition al, with sarenu leviyenu kohaneinu as its subject, naming who stands upon the sealed document rather than performing a third verbal act. That same formula — preposition plus definite passive participle plus officer list — repeats across the seam at the next verse's opening, “וְעַ֖ל הַחֲתוּמִ֑ים” ("and upon the sealed ones") — WEB "Now those who sealed were: Nehemiah the governor..." — with the participle shifting singular to plural rather than being reprised verbatim (the two forms differ in number and vocalization; the active-participle spelling that would make either an agent-noun, chotem, is unattested anywhere in the book, sweep: 0). The unnamed, class-only naming here (sarenu/leviyenu/kohaneinu, no proper noun) is itself what keeps this verse its own decision rather than the incipit of the sealers' list that follows: 10:1 (MT 10:2) immediately switches register to a named roster beginning with Nehemiah and Zedekiah, so the resolve-and-naming-of-classes verse and the named-roster verse are different kinds of text even though the same passive-participle formula bridges them. This sits at the live crux at the MT chapter break itself; that division is tier-4 versification metadata, playing no role in the argument above, which rests on the unnamed-classes-to-named-roster participant shift: this verse's resolve names only classes (sarenu/leviyenu/kohaneinu), while the next verse's roster opens by naming individuals, Nehemiah then Zedekiah. The koretim/kotvim performative bicolon marks this verse's own act of cutting and writing the covenant; the hechatum/hachatumim passive-participle repetition across the seam is a conceded continuity in sealing vocabulary that this row answers rather than a warrant it relies on, since that same bridge argues at least as strongly for tight forward binding as for a standalone hinge. A petuchah (PE, single-witness) falls at oshb:Neh.9.37, this row's own front seam; per this book's Writings tier-3 policy it corroborates only weakly, is never a boundary driver, and its absence would not have counted against the boundary either way.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 9:38 as the closing cadence of the great prayer loses because nothing in it addresses God or petitions; its grammar is resultative throughout, and its one distinctive noun is picked up again in the roster that follows, not anywhere back in the prayer. The more genuinely live rival is forward: folding 9:38 into the sealers' list that follows as that register's incipit rather than its own decision. That rival is real — the hechatum/hachatumim bridge argues at least as strongly for tight forward binding as for a standalone hinge — but 9:38 itself names no individual (just the classes sarenu/leviyenu/kohaneinu), while 10:1 (MT 10:2) opens by naming Nehemiah and Zedekiah at its head; the unnamed communal resolve and the named roster are different participant classes bridged by, but not merged under, the shared sealing vocabulary.

boundary_rationale: WEB "Now those who sealed were: Nehemiah the governor, the son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah," runs a bare name-chain through v.7, then v.8 closes: "Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah. These were the priests." The unit opens where it does because MT 10:2 (WEB 10:1) opens with “וְעַ֖ל הַחֲתוּמִ֑ים” ("and upon the sealed ones"), resuming the identical preposition-plus-passive-participle formula that closes MT 10:1 (WEB 9:38), “וְעַל֙ הֶֽחָת֔וּם” ("and upon the sealed [thing]") — the same hechatum/hachatumim bridge argued from the seam's other edge at 9:38 itself — with the participle shifting singular to plural (sweep: 1 verse book-wide for hachatumim, MT 10.2) as this roster's own opening warrant. The named chain beginning here (Nehemiah, then Zedekiah) also completes the shift from unnamed, class-only naming (sarenu/leviyenu/kohaneinu) to a named roster — the discriminator 9:38's own decision rests its boundary on — so the seam's two markers point the same direction without collision: the formula bridges the seam, while the naming shift is what the seam's far side treats as decisive. The Hebrew closing label is “אֵ֖לֶּה הַכֹּהֲנִֽים” ("these [are] the priests") — an explicit, named class-tag rather than a bare list terminus, and the collocation of elleh with a priestly-class noun stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide: this one and 12:1's “וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים” ("now these are the priests"), which OPENS a register rather than closing one. The genuine rear-facing comparandum for this row's colophon function is 12:26's “אֵ֕לֶּה בִּימֵ֛י” ("these were in the days of..."), which closes the clergy register the same way this verse closes the priestly sealers; the shared elleh+kohanim wording at 12:1 cuts the other way and is not the intended analogy. A setumah (single-witness) follows this exact verse (oshb:Neh.10.9; zone-interior, cited with its WEB 10:8 alias), landing precisely at the label rather than mid-list — weak corroboration, but placed exactly where the tag falls.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through the Levite names (into WEB 10:9) loses because the text itself supplies an explicit closing tag ("these were the priests") that the Levite list, opening fresh in the next verse, does not share.

boundary_rationale: WEB "The Levites: Jeshua the son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel;" through "Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu." opens with its own named class, the Hebrew “וְֽהַלְוִיִּ֑ם וְיֵשׁ֨וּעַ֙” ("and the Levites, Jeshua") — the conjunction on vehalviyim is real, and a second waw follows on the first name itself (contra a prior asyndetic label, which in fact belongs to “רָאשֵׁ֖י הָעָ֑ם” at 10:14, the lay-heads heading the next verse, carrying neither vav nor article, doubly asyndetic against its own first name “פַּרְעֹשׁ֙”); read alone, both conjunctions are the natural evidence for the rival that the Levites simply continue the priestly sealers' chain rather than opening a class of their own. What still marks this as a header despite the conjunction is the function it shares with rashei ha'am — a verse-initial class noun standing outside, and governing, the apposed name list that follows it, distinct from the priestly names themselves and from the closing label seen in row 02 (“אֵ֖לֶּה הַכֹּהֲנִֽים”) — not the conjunction itself: unlike rashei ha'am's doubly asyndetic opener, the waw here on both vehalviyim and its first name is not part of the parallel, and is conceded rather than explained away. A setumah (single-witness) sits at the front seam (oshb:Neh.10.9, WEB 10:8, closing the priests) and another setumah (single-witness) at the rear seam (oshb:Neh.10.14, WEB 10:13) — both zone-interior, both weak corroboration, but symmetric on both edges of this unit. The unit ends at 10:13 because the next verse changes vocabulary entirely, from named Levitical clan-heads to a fresh class-heading.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this Levite sub-list into the priests' row is a real rival precisely because vehalviyim's own conjunctive waw could read as continuing the prior list; it still loses because the class-noun-plus-apposed-list shape parallels rashei ha'am's header at 10:14 rather than any priestly-name continuation, and the closing tag of row 02 (elleh hakohanim) has already sealed that list shut.

boundary_rationale: WEB "The chiefs of the people: Parosh, Pahathmoab, Elam, Zattu, Bani," opens a third named class; the Hebrew רָאשֵׁ֖י הָעָ֑ם ("heads of the people") is a distinct title from both "the priests" and "the Levites," marking lay clan-heads specifically. A setumah (single-witness) closes the Levite class immediately before this row begins (oshb:Neh.10.14, WEB 10:13) — front-seam corroboration; no mark follows 10:27 itself, and mark absence carries no evidentiary weight against a boundary here. The row runs through "Malluch, Harim, and Baanah" because the next verse (WEB 10:28) drops the bare name-chain register entirely for a discourse sentence naming groups rather than individuals.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this row with the community-adjuration verses that follow loses because 10:14-27 is still individual-name listing (the sealed-roster genre), while 10:28 shifts to describing collective classes in running prose.

boundary_rationale: WEB "The rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and all those who had separated themselves..." shifts subject with the Hebrew “וּשְׁאָ֣ר הָעָ֡ם” ("and the rest of the people"), followed by an enumerated class-list “הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים הַ֠לְוִיִּם הַשּׁוֹעֲרִ֨ים הַמְשֹׁרְרִ֜ים הַנְּתִינִ֗ים” (the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the Nethinim) that names GROUPS, not individuals — a different register from the roster in rows 02-04, and containing zero personal names. The notice continues into v.29 with the participle chain “מַחֲזִיקִ֣ים עַל אֲחֵיהֶם֮ אַדִּירֵיהֶם֒ וּבָאִ֞ים בְּאָלָ֣ה וּבִשְׁבוּעָ֗ה” (web:Neh.10.29 "joined with their brothers, their nobles, and entered into a curse and into an oath") — two participles, not a finite adjuration verb, describing the subject before the oath's content is even stated. This notice closes here, before WEB 10:30's obligations proper, on a grammatical rather than topical seam: MT 10:29-30's matrix clauses run entirely on participles (“מַחֲזִיקִ֣ים”, "holding fast"; “וּבָאִ֞ים”, "entering") and infinitives construct (“לָלֶ֨כֶת֙”, "to walk"; “וְלִשְׁמ֣וֹר וְלַעֲשׂ֗וֹת”, "and to observe and do"); the span's one finite verb sits inside the relative clause “אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִתְּנָ֔ה בְּיַ֖ד מֹשֶׁ֣ה” ("which was given by the hand of Moses") modifying torat ha-Elohim, not on the notice's own main line. The shift from that participial subject-description to the finite 1cp obligations opening at WEB 10:30 (MT 10:31), “נִתֵּ֥ן” ("we will give"), marks the seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 10:28-29 as part of the named-sealers roster is excluded on inspection — zero personal names occur in either verse — so rejecting that merge costs the row nothing. The genuinely live rival is forward: the oath introduced here, “וּבָאִ֞ים בְּאָלָ֣ה וּבִשְׁבוּעָ֗ה”, is completed in content by the asher-clause opening WEB 10:30 (MT 10:31) alone, “וַאֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא נִתֵּ֥ן בְּנֹתֵ֖ינוּ”, a dependency row 061 itself describes as directly extending this notice's oath-content. It still loses as a merger, though, on the participle-versus-finite-verb contrast: WEB 10:28-29 (MT 10:29-30) run on participles and infinitives describing who is bound and how, their one finite verb tucked inside the relative clause naming Moses' torah, while WEB 10:30 (MT 10:31) opens the finite 1cp obligations proper; that shift, not the oath's semantic continuation, is where the notice's grammar actually closes.

boundary_rationale: WEB "and that we would not give our daughters to the peoples of the land, nor take their daughters for our sons;" opens with the asher-clause “וַאֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא נִתֵּ֥ן בְּנֹתֵ֖ינוּ” ("and that we would not give our daughters"), directly extending the oath-content named at the end of row 05; va'asher itself stands in exactly 1 verse across the whole of MT chapter 10 (this one), so it names a single relative clause, not a recurring pattern. WEB 10:31 (MT 10:32) does not continue that construction: its Hebrew, “וְעַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֡רֶץ הַֽמְבִיאִים֩” ("and the peoples of the land who bring..."), is a fronted-nominal casus pendens with a participial modifier, resumed by its own apodosis, and carries zero occurrences of asher (WEB itself renders it "and if," not "and that"). What actually binds these two verses together is a different, repeated device: both verses carry the negated 1cp yiqtol lo nikkach ("we will not take"), MT 10:31's “וְאֶת בְּנֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א נִקַּ֖ח לְבָנֵֽינוּ” and MT 10:32's “לֹא נִקַּ֥ח מֵהֶ֛ם בַּשַּׁבָּ֖ת” (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, MT 10.31 and MT 10.32). MT 10:32 does not itself close on that negation: its own final clause turns to a second, positive 1cp pledge, “וְנִטֹּ֛שׁ אֶת הַשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖ית וּמַשָּׁ֥א כָל יָֽד” ("and we will forego the seventh year and the exaction of every debt", sweep: 1 verse book-wide for netosh, MT 10.32); that second pledge verb does not open a fresh construction the way MT 10:33's verb-initial vehe'emadnu does — it stays inside the same casus-pendens sentence begun by ve'amei ha'aretz, merely adding a further object within the same sentence — so the rear seam still falls at MT 10:33's fresh weqatal opener, not here. The unit ends here because v.32 (WEB) switches from casus-pendens/apodosis material spelling out the oath's content to a fresh 1cp performative, "Also we made ordinances for ourselves," introducing a new, self-imposed category of obligation with its own verb-initial main clause (“וְהֶעֱמַ֤דְנוּ”, independently attested as a singleton construction, sweep: 1) rather than continuing to unpack the existing oath.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying this row through the third-shekel pledge (WEB 10:32) loses the seam between the negated-yiqtol lo nikkach cohesion that binds 10:30-31 and the new verb-initial performative “וְהֶעֱמַ֤דְנוּ” ("and we established") that opens the next obligation as its own singleton construction (sweep: 1).

boundary_rationale: WEB "Also we made ordinances for ourselves, to charge ourselves yearly with the third part of a shekel for the service of the house of our God:" opens with the fresh performative וְהֶעֱמַ֤דְנוּ עָלֵ֨ינוּ֙ מִצְוֺ֔ת ("and we established upon ourselves commandments"), a main-clause resolve distinct from the asher-continuations in row 06. V.33 itemizes the tax's uses and closes, WEB "...and for all the work of the house of our God," Hebrew וְכֹ֖ל מְלֶ֥אכֶת בֵּית אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ ("and all the service of the house of our God"). A setumah (single-witness) follows this verse (oshb:Neh.10.34; zone-interior, WEB 10:33 alias) — the rear-seam corroboration for ending the tax-ordinance here, right before the wood-offering pledge begins its own fronted clause.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row into the wood-offering pledge (WEB 10:34) loses because that verse opens with its own fronted-object construction naming a different obligation (timber, not money), and a setumah (single-witness) falls at exactly this seam.

boundary_rationale: WEB "We, the priests, the Levites, and the people, cast lots for the wood offering..." opens with the fronted object construction וְהַגּוֹרָל֨וֹת הִפַּ֜לְנוּ ("and-the-lots we-cast"), a distinct clause-type from the tax-ordinance in row 07, corroborated by a setumah (single-witness) that immediately precedes it (oshb:Neh.10.34; WEB 10:33 alias — the front-seam mark, argued from this row's side of the boundary). The series continues through produce and livestock dedications and tithe pledges and closes with the covenant's pledge-close, WEB "We will not forsake the house of our God," Hebrew וְלֹ֥א נַעֲזֹ֖ב אֶת בֵּ֥ית אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ ("and we will not forsake the house of our God"). The root עזב ('forsake') forms a genuine 9-member verbal family book-wide — 3:8 ('they left off' building), 3:34/WEB 4:2 (Sanballat's taunt), 5:10 (a Qal cohortative, na'azvah na, 'let us forgo this debt-burden,' the same binyan as this verse's Qal yiqtol but differing in mood, not stem, and taking a different object), 9:17/9:19/9:31 (the Great Prayer's negated lo azavtam refrain), 9:28 (the same root's positive counterpart, vata'azvem, 'you left them'), 10:40 (this verse), and 13:11 (a genuine Niphal, ne'ezav, 'the house of God was forsaken,' thematically resonant but grammatically distinct) — plus one skeleton-only false positive, the proper name “עַזְבּ֔וּק” ('Azbuk') at 3:16, for 10 contiguous-substring hits in total (sweep: 10); a narrower 3-hit figure belongs only to the tighter na'azov-family substring (5:10/10:40/13:11), not to the root. Because the Great Prayer's own three-fold negated refrain (9:17, 9:19, 9:31) is the closest and most consequential echo of this verse's resolve, distinctiveness is argued instead on the exact collocation: lo na'azov et-beit eloheinu, sweep: 1 verse book-wide (MT 10.40), and it is this specific documentary resolve — echoing, not repeating, the prayer's plea-register refrain — that closes the obligations document here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the wood-offering, produce-dedication, and tithe clauses at WEB 10:37/10:38 is the genuinely live rival: MT 10:38 (WEB 10:37) ends with a third-person aside, “וְהֵם֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם הַֽמְעַשְּׂרִ֔ים” ("and they, the Levites, are the ones tithing"), and MT 10:39 (WEB 10:38) opens with a weqatal carrying a fresh 3ms subject, “וְהָיָ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֧ן” ("and the priest ... shall be"), continuing in third-person prescription (“יַעֲל֨וּ”, “יָבִ֨יאוּ”) through most of MT 10:39-40 — exactly the kind of fresh, subject-shifting opener the series otherwise lacks. It still holds together as one unit because the 1cp resolve returns in the verse's final clause, “וְלֹ֥א נַעֲזֹ֖ב אֶת בֵּ֥ית אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ”, folding the third-person prescriptive material back under the same 1cp voice that opened the pledge series at 10:34's “וְהַגּוֹרָל֨וֹת הִפַּ֜לְנוּ” (ve'hagoralot hipalnu).

boundary_rationale: WEB "The princes of the people lived in Jerusalem." opens with “וַיֵּשְׁב֥וּ שָׂרֵֽי הָעָ֖ם בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם” ("and the princes of the people dwelt in Jerusalem"), then narrates the lottery itself, “וּשְׁאָ֣ר הָ֠עָם הִפִּ֨ילוּ גוֹרָל֜וֹת” ("and the rest of the people cast lots"). V.2 closes the notice with its resolution, “וַֽיְבָרֲכ֖וּ הָעָ֑ם לְכֹל֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים הַמִּֽתְנַדְּבִ֔ים” ("and the people blessed all the men who volunteered"), before a petuchah (single-witness) at oshb:Neh.11.2; what binds this resolution to v.1's lottery is not an assumed identity between the volunteers and the men the lot fell upon, but the shared purpose infinitive both verses close on: v.1's “לָשֶׁ֨בֶת֙ בִּֽירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙” names the lot's own purpose and v.2's “לָשֶׁ֖בֶת בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם” ("to dwell in Jerusalem," sweep: 2 verses book-wide) closes the couplet on the identical clause, binding blessing to lottery without asserting that the volunteers and the lot-chosen are the same men. The obligations document has just ended in named documentary "we"-pledges; this couplet narrates a lottery in third-person past-tense report, a different discourse mode that argues for treating it as its own brief unit rather than folding it into either row 08 or the superscription in row 10.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 11:1-2 forward to the WEB 11:3 superscription as one continuous register-opening remains a genuine, conceded overlap in theme — 11:1 already narrates princes dwelling in Jerusalem in terms close to what 11:3 restates — but it is answered by form rather than left merely open: 11:3 opens with its own demonstrative-plus-class-title incipit, “וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ רָאשֵׁ֣י הַמְּדִינָ֔ה” ("and these are the heads of the province"), the same construction as the golah register header “אֵ֣לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י הַמְּדִינָ֗ה” ("these are the children of the province") at 7:6 (the class noun hamedinah: 2 verses book-wide; the full incipit collocation at 11:3 itself: a singleton, sweep: 1), marking 11:3 as a fresh register head rather than a continuation of 11:1's narrative report. The split is still argued at medium_low, since the thematic overlap remains real even where the form-based answer resolves the segmentation question.

boundary_rationale: WEB "Now these are the chiefs of the province who lived in Jerusalem; but in the cities of Judah, everyone lived in his possession in their cities-Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple servants, and the children of Solomon's servants." opens with וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ רָאשֵׁ֣י הַמְּדִינָ֔ה ("and these [are] heads of the province"), a formula that echoes 11:1's report but is not identical: 11:1 uses sarei ha'am ("princes of the people"); this verse uses rashei ha-medinah ("heads of the province"). The clause that follows, וּבְעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה יָֽשְׁב֞וּ אִ֤ישׁ בַּאֲחֻזָּתוֹ֙ בְּעָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם ("and in the cities of Judah they dwelt, each in his holding, in their cities"), takes as its delayed subject -- no intervening verb -- the five-class inventory יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל הַכֹּהֲנִים֙ וְהַלְוִיִּ֣ם וְהַנְּתִינִ֔ים וּבְנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹֽה ("Israel, the priests, the Levites, the nethinim, and the sons of Solomon's servants"): a population enumeration, not a table of contents for the register that follows. That register both adds classes the inventory omits (gatekeepers at 11:19, singers at 11:22-23) and never again names one it includes (sons of Solomon's servants, sweep: 3 book-wide, none after this verse). The same cities-of-Judah topic is what 11:20 resumes (sweep: arei Yehudah, 2 book-wide, only 11:3 and 11:20), so this verse opens the frame that 11:20 closes. A petuchah (single-witness) precedes it (oshb:Neh.11.2), closing the lot-casting report before this superscription begins, and the province-header formula itself parallels, well beyond this immediate seam, the header function a comparable formula serves for the golah list many chapters earlier at oshb:Neh.7.6.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 11:3 as merely resuming 11:1's report (so the two rows should be one) loses because the vocabulary shift (rashei ha-medinah, not sarei ha'am) marks a fresh formula opening the settlers account; reading its five-class inventory as a table of contents for the register that follows also loses, since the register both adds classes the inventory omits (gatekeepers, singers) and drops one it names (sons of Solomon's servants) -- the inventory belongs instead to the cities-of-Judah frame this verse opens and 11:20 closes.

boundary_rationale: WEB "Some of the children of Judah and of the children of Benjamin lived in Jerusalem. Of the children of Judah: Athaiah..." opens with וּבִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ יָֽשְׁב֔וּ ("and in Jerusalem dwelt") then names the class, מִבְּנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וּמִבְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן מִבְּנֵ֣י יְ֠הוּדָה ("of the sons of Judah and of the sons of Benjamin, of the sons of Judah"). The Judah genealogy runs through v.6, which supplies its own closing count, WEB "were four hundred sixty-eight valiant men," Hebrew אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֛וֹת שִׁשִּׁ֥ים וּשְׁמֹנָ֖ה אַנְשֵׁי חָֽיִל ("four hundred sixty-eight men of valor") after naming the whole clan, כָּל בְּנֵי פֶ֕רֶץ הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם ("all sons of Perez who dwelt in Jerusalem"). A setumah (single-witness) follows this verse (oshb:Neh.11.6), closing the Judah class before the Benjamin class opens fresh in v.7.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping Judah and Benjamin as one lay-settlers row loses the closing-total pattern (each clan gets its own head-count) and the corroborating mark that separates them, the same class-by-count structure seen in the priestly and Levitical sub-lists later in this chapter.

boundary_rationale: WEB "These are the sons of Benjamin: Sallu..." opens with וְאֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן סַלֻּ֡א ("and these [are] sons of Benjamin: Sallu"), the same ve'elleh ("and these") header-formula as the superscription at 11:3, now scoped to one clan. A setumah (single-witness) immediately precedes this verse (oshb:Neh.11.6, closing Judah). The unit runs through v.9's overseer notice, WEB "Joel the son of Zichri was their overseer; and Judah the son of Hassenuah was second over the city," Hebrew וְיוֹאֵ֥ל בֶּן זִכְרִ֖י פָּקִ֣יד עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם ("and Joel son of Zichri, overseer over them") and וִיהוּדָ֧ה בֶן הַסְּנוּאָ֛ה עַל הָעִ֖יר מִשְׁנֶֽה ("and Judah son of Hassenuah, over the city, second"), closed by a petuchah (single-witness) at oshb:Neh.11.9.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the overseer notice (v.9) into its own row loses because it names no new resident class -- it is an administrative coda to the Benjamin count, paralleled by the paqid-aleihem overseer note closing the priestly sub-list alone (11:14, Zabdiel; sweep: paqid, 4 book-wide -- 11:9, 11:14, 11:22, 12:42). The Levitical sub-list closes instead with a bare grand total (11:18); its own overseer notice, וּפְקִ֤יד הַלְוִיִּם֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם עֻזִּ֤י ("and overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem, Uzzi"), sits inside the temple-personnel appendix (11:22), three verses past the Levites' own close, and uses a construct chain (u-fqid ha-Leviyyim), not this verse's paqid-aleihem collocation.

boundary_rationale: WEB "Of the priests: Jedaiah the son of Joiarib, Jachin," opens with מִן הַֽכֹּהֲנִ֑ים ("from/of the priests"), a min-partitive header sharing its family with Judah's own opener (11:4, מִבְּנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה) and the Levites' (11:15, וּמִֽן הַלְוִיִּ֑ם); the same partitive also opens the Levite closing note at 11:36 (וּמִן הַלְוִיִּ֔ם). Of the settlers-and-clergy register's four opener families -- ve'elleh (sweep: 4 book-wide), min-partitive (sweep: 5 book-wide), vav+definite-class-noun (11:19 וְהַשּֽׁוֹעֲרִים֙, 11:21, 12:8), and kol+class-noun (11:18 כָּל הַלְוִיִּם֙) -- only Benjamin's own incipit (11:7, וְאֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן) uses ve'elleh; this verse's partitive is not distinct from a uniform lay-clan formula, since Judah, the register's earliest-listed lay clan, is itself partitive-headed. A petuchah (single-witness) that closes the Benjamin section (oshb:Neh.11.9) precedes it. Three named sub-groups follow with running totals (822, 242, 128), and the unit closes with its own overseer notice, WEB "and their overseer was Zabdiel, the son of Haggedolim," Hebrew וּפָקִ֣יד עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם זַבְדִּיאֵ֖ל בֶּן הַגְּדוֹלִֽים ("and overseer over them, Zabdiel son of Haggedolim"), the same paqid-aleihem collocation used for Benjamin's overseers at 11:9. A setumah (single-witness) follows this verse (oshb:Neh.11.14).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Rowing the three priestly sub-totals (822/242/128) separately loses because none of the three carries its own header or mark; they run as one partitive-headed class bounded by petuchah (single-witness) before and setumah (single-witness) after. Treating this partitive as a marker distinguishing the priests from a uniform lay-clan ve'elleh also loses: the register runs a ve'elleh/min-partitive alternation (ve'elleh at 11:3, 11:7 only; sweep: 4 book-wide), not a lay-vs-clergy split.

boundary_rationale: WEB "Of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub..." opens with וּמִֽן הַלְוִיִּ֑ם ("and of the Levites"), the same partitive header pattern as the priests' class at 11:10, following a setumah (single-witness) that closes it (oshb:Neh.11.14). The unit closes with its own grand total, unlike the priests' running sub-counts: WEB "All the Levites in the holy city were two hundred eighty-four," Hebrew כָּל הַלְוִיִּם֙ בְּעִ֣יר הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ מָאתַ֖יִם שְׁמֹנִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָֽה ("all the Levites in the holy city: two hundred eighty-four"), followed by a petuchah (single-witness) at oshb:Neh.11.18.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row to include the gatekeepers (WEB 11:19) loses because the Levites already close with their own summary total and a petuchah (single-witness), and the gatekeepers open with a distinct class-name of their own.

boundary_rationale: WEB "Moreover the gatekeepers, Akkub, Talmon, and their brothers, who kept watch at the gates, were one hundred seventy-two." opens וְהַשּֽׁוֹעֲרִים֙ עַקּ֣וּב טַלְמ֔וֹן ("and the gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon"), a fourth named class following a petuchah (single-witness) that closed the Levites (oshb:Neh.11.18), and supplies its own count in the same verse, מֵאָ֖ה שִׁבְעִ֥ים וּשְׁנָֽיִם ("one hundred seventy-two"). No mark follows this verse, which is not counterevidence here; the row stands on the class-name-plus-count pattern shared with every other sub-list in this register (the priests' at 11:14, the Levites' at 11:18), here compressed into a single verse -- a textual fact about this entry's length, not a claim about the gatekeeper class's actual size relative to the others.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the gatekeepers into the Levite row loses their distinct class-name (hashsho'arim, applied to a separate group from the Levites in this list) and their own separately-counted total.

boundary_rationale: WEB "The residue of Israel, of the priests, and the Levites were in all the cities of Judah, everyone in his inheritance." opens וּשְׁאָ֨ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים הַלְוִיִּם֙ בְּכָל עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה אִ֖ישׁ בְּנַחֲלָתֽוֹ ("and the rest of Israel, the priests, the Levites, in all the cities of Judah, each in his inheritance"), a generic distributive statement with no named individual and no head-count, unlike every class-entry from 11:4 through 11:19. Grammatically it summarizes the whole preceding census (those not resident in Jerusalem specifically). The verse closes an inclusio with the register's own opening at 11:3: both share the Israel/priests/Levites class-sequence and an ish-be-X-o distributive clause, in chiastically inverted order -- 11:3 states the cities-clause then the class-list (וּבְעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה יָֽשְׁב֞וּ אִ֤ישׁ בַּאֲחֻזָּתוֹ֙ בְּעָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל הַכֹּהֲנִים֙ וְהַלְוִיִּ֣ם וְהַנְּתִינִ֔ים וּבְנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹֽה), 11:20 states the class-list then the cities-clause -- and the phrase arei Yehudah is otherwise unique to these two verses (sweep: 2 book-wide). The opening וּשְׁאָ֨ר ("the rest") additionally ties this verse to the same root construction used at 11:1's report and at 10:28 (sweep: 3 book-wide). A forward reading is available -- 11:20's cities-of-Judah topic anticipates the one 11:25 opens with its own header, וְאֶל הַחֲצֵרִ֖ים בִּשְׂדֹתָ֑ם מִבְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה ("and as for the villages in their fields, some of the sons of Judah"), matching 11:4's own partitive-plus-dwelling opener -- but it is not adopted: 11:25 is independently self-headed and needs no assist from 11:20, while 11:20's inverted-order echo of 11:3 is a closing-bracket signature a forward heading for 11:25 would not carry. This verse functions as a colophon rather than another named entry; it is followed immediately by fresh, specifically-named notices (temple servants, a Levite overseer, singers, a royal deputy) that resume individual naming.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching this verse to the gatekeepers' entry (11:19) loses because it names no individual and gives no count -- its "everyone in his inheritance" is a summary formula closing the census, not a fifth counted class. Reading it instead as heading the Judah-village material that follows (11:20's cities-of-Judah clause anticipating 11:25's own header) also loses: 11:25 carries its own independent opener matching 11:4's, needing no assist from 11:20, while 11:20's inverted-order echo of 11:3 (class-list + distributive clause, chiastically reversed) is a closing-bracket signature a forward heading would not carry.

boundary_rationale: WEB "But the temple servants lived in Ophel; and Ziha and Gishpa were over the temple servants." opens וְהַנְּתִינִ֖ים יֹשְׁבִ֣ים בָּעֹ֑פֶל וְצִיחָ֥א וְגִשְׁפָּ֖א עַל הַנְּתִינִֽים ("and the temple-servants dwelt in Ophel, and Ziha and Gishpa over the temple-servants") after the colophon at 11:20; its first clause (class-noun + participle + place) continues the register's own dwelling-verb thread (11:1, 11:3, 11:4, 11:25; sweep: 8 book-wide), while its second clause opens the appointment-naming that structures the rest of the unit. Two more named appointments follow: the Levite overseer — web:Neh.11.22 “The overseer also of the Levites at Jerusalem was Uzzi the son of Bani…” — Hebrew וּפְקִ֤יד הַלְוִיִּם֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם עֻזִּ֤י ("and overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem, Uzzi"), grounded by the ki-clause at v23, כִּֽי מִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַאֲמָנָ֥ה עַל הַמְשֹׁרְרִ֖ים ("for the king's command was upon them, and a provision for the singers") -- a subordinate ground, not a further appointee -- and the royal deputy, WEB "Pethahiah the son of Meshezabel...was at the king's hand in all matters concerning the people," Hebrew וּפְתַֽחְיָ֨ה בֶּן מְשֵֽׁיזַבְאֵ֜ל ("and Pethahiah son of Meshezabel") and לְיַ֣ד הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְכָל דָּבָ֖ר לָעָֽם ("at the king's hand for every matter concerning the people"). These three named appointments (Ziha/Gishpa, Uzzi, Pethahiah) share a "named person(s) over/responsible-for X" pattern distinct from both the counted classes above and the village list that follows at WEB 11:25; grouping them keeps that shared administrative-notice function together rather than imposing a count-based class boundary the text does not supply for any of the three.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the Nethinim notice (11:21) from the Levite-overseer/singers/royal-deputy notices (11:22-24) at the petuchah (single-witness) that follows oshb:Neh.11.21 is a live option, since that mark does fall inside this row, and 11:21 is itself formally split (a residence clause continuing the register's dwelling thread, then a separate appointment clause); the absence of a head-count or fresh class-name at that point is not by itself decisive -- 11:20 was accepted as its own unit under the same absence -- but no literary-type shift separates the residence/appointment seam the way one separates 071 from its neighbors, so the four verses are kept together as one administrative appendix rather than pressed into a further split the content does not clearly demand.

boundary_rationale: WEB "As for the villages with their fields, some of the children of Judah lived in Kiriath Arba and its towns..." opens וְאֶל הַחֲצֵרִ֖ים בִּשְׂדֹתָ֑ם מִבְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה יָֽשְׁב֞וּ ("and as for the villages with their fields, some of the sons of Judah dwelt"), a fresh discourse unit (villages-with-fields, not Jerusalem residency) following the temple-personnel appointment notices at 11:21 through 11:24. It closes with its own summary, WEB "So they encamped from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom," Hebrew וַיַּחֲנ֥וּ מִבְּאֵֽר שֶׁ֖בַע עַד גֵּֽיא הִנֹּֽם ("and they encamped from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom"), before the Benjamin village list opens fresh with its own named subject at 11:31.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Running the Judah and Benjamin village lists together as one row loses the closing geographic summary that marks off Judah's villages specifically, and the fresh subject-headed opening ("the children of Benjamin also...") that begins the next tribe's list.

boundary_rationale: WEB "The children of Benjamin also lived from Geba onward, at Michmash and Aija..." opens וּבְנֵ֥י בִנְיָמִ֖ן מִגָּ֑בַע ("and sons of Benjamin from Geba"), naming a fresh tribal subject after Judah's closing summary at 11:25 through 11:30. The village-name chain runs through v.35, and the part closes with a short Levite note, WEB "Of the Levites, certain divisions in Judah settled in Benjamin's territory," Hebrew וּמִן הַלְוִיִּ֔ם מַחְלְק֥וֹת יְהוּדָ֖ה לְבִנְיָמִֽין ("and of the Levites, divisions of Judah [attached] to Benjamin"), marked by a petuchah (single-witness) at oshb:Neh.11.36. This closing note opens with the same u-min partitive used at the priests' (11:10, מִן הַֽכֹּהֲנִ֑ים) and Levites' (11:15, וּמִֽן הַלְוִיִּ֑ם) own class-headers -- one of this register's four opener families (ve'elleh, sweep: 4 book-wide; min-partitive, sweep: 5 book-wide; vav+definite-class-noun, 11:19/11:21/12:8; kol+class-noun, 11:18) -- so it is not device-bare. What keeps it with the Benjamin village list rather than as its own register is topical, not formulaic: unlike 11:10 and 11:15, where the identical partitive introduces a named roster, 11:36 is a single verbless clause naming no individual -- a one-verse appendix to the just-completed geography, not a new register.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Giving the Levite note (11:36) its own row is a live alternative worth taking seriously, since 11:36 does carry a genuine class-header partitive, not a bare fragment; it is not adopted because the note names no individual and supplies no verb of dwelling, unlike every roster the same partitive elsewhere introduces (11:10, 11:15) -- it is one verse of trailing information, not a register in its own right.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the joint roll-call header וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם (web:Neh.12.1; WEB “Now these are the priests and the Levites who went up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua”), which names both clergy classes but the roll that actually follows (1b-7a) names priests, not Levites. The unit is its own bracket: "elleh" opens v1 and returns at the close, אֵ֣לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֧י הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים וַאֲחֵיהֶ֖ם בִּימֵ֥י יֵשֽׁוּעַ (web:Neh.12.7; WEB “These were the chiefs of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Jeshua.”). The Levites proper get their own header at v8 ("Moreover the Levites were"), so the priestly roll's elleh...elleh inclusio is the tighter edge, not the coarser "returnee clergy vv1-9" grouping.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 12.1-9 as one row conflates the priestly roll's own elleh...elleh inclusio with the Levites' separate class header at v8.

boundary_rationale: Verse 8 opens its own class header, וְהַלְוִיִּ֗ם יֵשׁ֧וּעַ בִּנּ֛וּי קַדְמִיאֵ֥ל (web:Neh.12.8; WEB "Moreover the Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel"), distinct from the priestly roll's own anaphoric closer at v7b, אֵ֣לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֧י הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים ("these are the chiefs of the priests"), which restricts the preceding roll to priests. The two-verse entry closes at v9 with the antiphonal-arrangement term לְנֶגְדָּ֖ם (web:Neh.12.9; WEB "were close to them according to their offices"); the same watch-arrangement term recurs at 12:24 describing the Levite chiefs' arrangement (sweep: 2 book-wide: 12:9, 12:24), tying this entry forward to that later verse. MT 12:9 carries a ketiv/qere pair on the name Unni (וענו וְעֻנִּ֧י; WEB follows the ketiv, "Unno") -- disclosed here as the verse is quoted/spanned. A petuchah (PE, single-witness) falls at oshb:Neh.12.7, exactly the v7/v8 seam this entry opens on; per this book's Writings tier-3 policy it corroborates only weakly and never drives the boundary, but it is present, not absent as a prior description had it -- the seam rests primarily on the v7b closer and v8's fresh class-noun, with the mark as tier-3 corroboration for it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding vv8-9 back into a single 12.1-9 "returnee clergy" row erases the vehalevi'im class-header shift and the shared watch-arrangement vocabulary that ties this entry forward to 12:24.

boundary_rationale: A new genre marker opens the unit: the patronymic chain formula וְיֵשׁ֖וּעַ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת יֽוֹיָקִ֑ים (web:Neh.12.10; WEB “Jeshua became the father of Joiakim”) repeats holid et three more times across the two verses (four occurrences total: twice in v10, twice in v11), a begetting-chain syntax distinct from the roll-call apposition the surrounding rows use instead (vv1-9, 12-26 name officeholders without tracing descent). The third link, Elyashiv to Yoiada, elides the verb entirely (וְאֶלְיָשִׁ֖יב אֶת יוֹיָדָֽע, the bare object-marker standing for it) -- a gap that is itself part of the chain's formal texture, not a defect in the text. The chain runs exactly five links to its terminus, וְיוֹנָתָ֖ן הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת יַדּֽוּעַ (web:Neh.12.11; WEB “and Jonathan became the father of Jaddua”), after which v12 opens a fresh "in the days of PN" list format, supplying the closing edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging the succession chain into the surrounding rosters would blur a distinct genealogical form with the roll-call forms bracketing it on both sides.

boundary_rationale: Opens with וּבִימֵי֙ יֽוֹיָקִ֔ים הָי֥וּ כֹהֲנִ֖ים רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֑וֹת (web:Neh.12.12; WEB “In the days of Joiakim were priests, heads of fathers' households”), a generation-marker header that answers v7's closing "bimey...Yeshua" with the next reign. The list restates the Jeshua-era roll of 12:1b-7a (22 names once v1b's three -- שְׂרָיָ֥ה יִרְמְיָ֖ה עֶזְרָֽא (Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra) -- are counted; vv2-7 alone hold 19) as 21 lamed-headed courses here (counting each ketiv/qere doublet once -- 12:14 למלוכי לִמְלִ֨יכוּ֙, 12:16 לעדיא לְעִדּ֥וֹא -- the token count is 23, the course count 21), matching the earlier roll name-for-name in sequence with eight orthographic variants (e.g. 12:2's מַלּ֖וּךְ answered by 12:14's לִמְלִ֨יכוּ֙) and חַטּֽוּשׁ (Hattush) at 12:2 alone unmatched under that standard, now paired with each course's head under Joiakim (a lamed-prefixed correlation, e.g. 13 "of Ezra, Meshullam"; though לְמִ֨נְיָמִ֔ין לְמוֹעַדְיָ֖ה פִּלְטָֽי at v17 leaves Miniamin with no head paired to it, Piltai pairing instead with the following Moadiah), a format distinct from both the plain roll of 1-7 and the begetting-chain of 10-11. It runs through v21, since v22 opens a THIRD generation-marker header ("the Levites, in the days of Eliashib..."), which supplies the closing edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 12.1-26 as one long clergy-list row would erase the three-generation bimey-PN header sequence (Jeshua / Joiakim / Eliashib) that actually structures the section.

boundary_rationale: Opens the third generation-marker, הַלְוִיִּם֩ בִּימֵ֨י אֶלְיָשִׁ֜יב (web:Neh.12.22; WEB “As for the Levites, in the days of Eliashib”) -- naming, across the verse, four names -- Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, Jaddua -- that continue the succession chain at 12:10-11 through its generations three to six on the identification of v22's יוֹחָנָן֙ (Johanan) with the chain's fifth link, 12:11's יוֹנָתָ֔ן (Jonathan) -- and immediately shifts register voice from roster-listing to archival citation: v23 names its own written source, כְּתוּבִ֕ים עַל סֵ֖פֶר דִּבְרֵ֣י הַיָּמִ֑ים (web:Neh.12.23; WEB “were written in the book of the chronicles”), a source-citation formula absent from 1-21. The same verse's own interior terminus, וְעַד יְמֵ֖י יֽוֹחָנָ֥ן בֶּן אֶלְיָשִֽׁיב (WEB “even until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib”), dates the archive one generation short of v22's own list (which continues through Jaddua) -- an interior marker, not itself a bracket edge, that fixes the citation's own historical horizon distinct from either v22's opening or v26's closing colophon. The note closes not with an inclusio answering v22 but with a colophon reaching back across the whole clergy-lists section: אֵ֕לֶּה בִּימֵ֛י יוֹיָקִ֥ים בֶּן יֵשׁ֖וּעַ בֶּן יוֹצָדָ֑ק וּבִימֵי֙ נְחֶמְיָ֣ה הַפֶּחָ֔ה וְעֶזְרָ֥א הַכֹּהֵ֖ן הַסּוֹפֵֽר (web:Neh.12.26; WEB “These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest and scribe”) names Joiakim, generation two -- the same Joiakim heading the courses header at 12:12 -- an earlier generation than v22's own opening, anchoring the whole clergy-lists section running from 12:1 forward -- not just this unit -- to the book's two protagonists just before the dedication opens. The pe (single-witness) keyed to 12:22 (a mark follows the verse it keys) falls between v22 and v23, interior to this span, not at its opening edge; the pe (single-witness) at v26 alone marks the section's actual close -- weak corroboration, not a driver.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 22-26 as a mere coda to 12.12-21 misses the archival source-citation shift at v23, which changes register voice rather than simply continuing the priestly-courses list.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the dedication frame וּבַחֲנֻכַּ֞ת חוֹמַ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם בִּקְשׁ֤וּ אֶת הַלְוִיִּם֙ (web:Neh.12.27; WEB “At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, they sought the Levites”), third person throughout the summons (27-29) and purification (30). It closes at וַיִּֽטַּהֲר֔וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֑ם וַֽיְטַהֲרוּ֙ אֶת הָעָ֔ם וְאֶת הַשְּׁעָרִ֖ים וְאֶֽת הַחוֹמָֽה (web:Neh.12.30; WEB “The priests and the Levites purified themselves; and they purified the people, the gates, and the wall”), the closing third-person clause of the summons before the memoir "I" resumes at v31. The edge is a person-shift, not a topic change: v31 continues the very same dedication event but switches into Nehemiah's own voice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Running 27-30 straight into the procession as one 12.27-43 row obscures the third-person-to-memoir-voice seam that the text itself marks at v31.

boundary_rationale: Opens on a 3mp-to-1cs person shift against an unbroken wayyiqtol chain: 12:30's וַיִּֽטַּהֲר֔וּ and 12:31's וָאַעֲלֶה֙ אֶת שָׂרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה מֵעַ֖ל לַחוֹמָ֑ה וָאַעֲמִ֡ידָה שְׁתֵּ֣י תוֹדֹת֩ גְּדוֹלֹ֨ת (web:Neh.12.31; WEB “Then I brought the princes of Judah up on the wall, and appointed two great companies”) carry straight through with no disjunctive waw, no date frame, and no new location -- the person shift alone marks the change here, setting Nehemiah's own action apart from the communal purification notice just closed. The memoir "I" recedes again through 12:32-37 (Hoshaiah's company roster given entirely in third person, no 1cs form) and resumes at 12:38's וַאֲנִ֣י אַחֲרֶ֑יהָ; that inset functions as a named-roster register, parallel to the ch.3/ch.7 conventions, traveling inside the single procession list v31 opens and v40 closes, so its own internal recession of "I" does not itself divide the scene. The two-company procession is bracketed by its own inclusio: "two great companies" here is answered at וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֛דְנָה שְׁתֵּ֥י הַתּוֹדֹ֖ת בְּבֵ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים (web:Neh.12.40; WEB “So the two companies of those who gave thanks in God's house stood”), which reunites both processions under the same numeral phrase named at the outset; the trumpeting priests and singers of 41-42 belong to that same convergence scene, and the unit closes on the celebration's own cadence, וַתִּשָּׁמַ֛ע שִׂמְחַ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם מֵרָחֽוֹק (web:Neh.12.43; WEB “so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard even far away”). No mark falls at this edge; a samekh (single-witness) keyed to 12:34 falls interior to the roster inset (32-37), a roster-internal mark of the ch.3/ch.7 class, not a boundary signal.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two rivals press against this edge. The stronger is upward attachment to the dedication complex opened at 12:27's וּבַחֲנֻכַּ֞ת חוֹמַ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם: 12:27-30 runs unbroken third person, so the shift to "I" really is new at 12:31, and neither the wayyiqtol chain nor the dedication frame breaks there; but a topical header naming an occasion is not a lexically closed bracket the way a repeated numeral phrase is, so it does not bind across an interior person shift -- here it is the person shift alone that marks the change, without any accompanying date, disjunctive, or locative change. The weaker rival, splitting at 12:38, targets the wrong signal: v38 reads וְהַתּוֹדָ֧ה הַשֵּׁנִ֛ית, an ordinal-singular "the second [company]," not a fresh two-choir reference, and a split there would still cut through the very "two companies...two companies" bracket binding v31 to v40 -- though v38 is where that inclusio argument is tested hardest, since a genuine person-shift return (va'ani achareha) sits there too, after the third-person roster inset of 32-37; there it is the lexically closed bracket, not the person-shift return, that keeps 31-43 one scene, because that closed bracket -- unlike the dedication header at 12:27 -- is the kind of signal that binds across an interior change.

boundary_rationale: Opens וַיִּפָּקְד֣וּ בַיּוֹם֩ הַה֨וּא אֲנָשִׁ֜ים עַל הַנְּשָׁכ֗וֹת לָא֨וֹצָר֥וֹת (web:Neh.12.44; WEB “On that day, men were appointed over the rooms for the treasures”), the second of three bayom hahu frames in the book (12:43, 12:44, 13:1; sweep: 3 book-wide). 12:43 and 12:44 stand adjacent, but the third, at 13:1, is separated from 12:44 by the intervening 12:45-47 notice, so the three span six verse positions, not three consecutive verses. The topic change does not rest on that adjacency or on word order -- 12:43's וַיִּזְבְּח֣וּ בַיּוֹם הַ֠הוּא and 12:44's וַיִּפָּקְד֣וּ בַיּוֹם֩ הַה֨וּא both place the verb before the frame -- but on verb class and subject: 12:44's niphal וַיִּפָּקְד֣וּ introduces an indefinite new participant set, אֲנָשִׁ֜ים, where 12:43 continues the sacrificial wayyiqtol chain of the same celebrants already in view, a genuine shift from dedication-day sacrifice to treasury-room administration, and a different scene again from 13:1's later Torah-reading notice. The unit runs to v47's Zerubbabel-to-Nehemiah summary of singer and gatekeeper portions, closing before 13:1 reopens its own bayom hahu for a different scene. A pe follows Neh.12.47 (single-witness).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 44-47 into the dedication on the strength of the shared bayom hahu wording would treat a recurring temporal frame as if it necessarily signals continuation, when here the verb class and subject shift -- niphal plus indefinite אֲנָשִׁ֜ים -- mark a change to cultic administration regardless of the frame's adjacency to 12:43.

boundary_rationale: Opens with בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא נִקְרָ֛א בְּסֵ֥פֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם (web:Neh.13.1; WEB “On that day they read in the book of Moses in the hearing of the people”), the third of three bayom hahu tokens in the book (12:43, 12:44, 13:1; sweep: 3 book-wide). 12:44 and 13:1 are not in tight succession -- the 12:45-47 notice intervenes -- so the topic-change reading rests on the register shift itself, not on adjacency: 13:1's impersonal niphal נִקְרָ֛א opening a public Torah-reading scene is a different scene type from 12:44-47's appointment notice. It closes with the vayehi kishmoa hinge וַיְהִ֖י כְּשָׁמְעָ֣ם אֶת הַתּוֹרָ֑ה וַיַּבְדִּ֥ילוּ כָל עֵ֖רֶב מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל (web:Neh.13.3; WEB “It came to pass, when they had heard the law, that they separated all the mixed multitude from Israel”), the same hearing-response frame that opens the book at 1:4 (sweep: 2 book-wide for vayehi+keshom-), here closing rather than opening a unit. Verse 13:4 then shifts register to a "before this" flashback (lifney mizzeh), a retrospective clause distinct from the bayom hahu frame just used.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Grouping 13.1-3 with 13.4-9 under one "Eliashib reforms" heading would merge a completed Torah-reading episode, closed by vayehi kishmoa, with a new "before this" flashback that explicitly reaches back in time.

boundary_rationale: Opens with a backward-looking frame, וְלִפְנֵ֣י מִזֶּ֔ה אֶלְיָשִׁיב֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן נָת֖וּן בְּלִשְׁכַּ֣ת בֵּית אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ (web:Neh.13.4; WEB “Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the rooms of the house of our God”), told in third person about Eliashib's misdeed (4-5). The memoir "I" does not resume until v6, to explain why Nehemiah had not known, וּבְכָל זֶ֕ה לֹ֥א הָיִ֖יתִי בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֡י בִּשְׁנַת֩ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וּשְׁתַּ֜יִם לְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֤סְתְּא מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶל֙ (web:Neh.13.6; WEB “But in all this, I was not at Jerusalem; for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon”), a dated parenthesis that explains rather than interrupts the "before this... I threw out... I commanded" action chain -- v8's grief-driven expulsion, וַיֵּ֥רַֽע לִ֖י מְאֹ֑ד וָֽאַשְׁלִ֜יכָה אֶֽת כָּל כְּלֵ֧י בֵית טוֹבִיָּ֛ה הַח֖וּץ מִן הַלִּשְׁכָּֽה (web:Neh.13.8; WEB “It grieved me severely. Therefore I threw all Tobiah's household stuff out of the room”) -- running to its close at וָאֹ֣מְרָ֔ה וַֽיְטַהֲר֖וּ הַלְּשָׁכ֑וֹת (web:Neh.13.9; WEB “Then I commanded, and they cleansed the rooms”). A pe follows Neh.13.9 (single-witness), coinciding with this close.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating the thirty-second-year note (6-7a) as its own row would sever the "I was absent, therefore I did not know, so when I returned I acted" causal chain the episode depends on.

boundary_rationale: Opens on a new perception-verb hinge, וָאֵ֣דְעָ֔ה כִּֽי מְנָי֥וֹת הַלְוִיִּ֖ם לֹ֣א נִתָּ֑נָה (web:Neh.13.10; WEB “I perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been given them”), moving from the finished chamber-cleansing to a fresh grievance. The treasurer appointment at v13, וְעַל יָדָ֔ם חָנָ֥ן (web:Neh.13.13; WEB “and next to them was Hanan”), uses "ve-al yadam" of Hanan's subordinate rank among the treasurers, not the chapter-3 wall-register connective of the same wording -- disambiguated here so the phrase is not mistaken for that device. The unit closes with זָכְרָה לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י עַל זֹ֑את (web:Neh.13.14; WEB “Remember me, my God, concerning this”), the second of four zokrah-li elohai closers in the book (sweep: 4 book-wide for zokrah-li; 6 book-wide for the refrain overall), echoing the first instance at 5:19.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through 13:22 as one long "Levite reforms" row would merge two structurally distinct episodes that each open on their own hinge and close on their own zokrah.

boundary_rationale: Opens with בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֡מָּה רָאִ֣יתִי בִֽיהוּדָ֣ה דֹּֽרְכִֽים גִּתּ֣וֹת בַּשַּׁבָּ֡ת (web:Neh.13.15; WEB “In those days I saw some men treading wine presses on the Sabbath in Judah”), the book's only bayamim hahemmah form (sweep: 1 book-wide, distinct from the two bayamim hahem instances at 6:17 and 13:23). The internal vayehi ka'asher beat at v19 (gate-closing enforcement) is one of eight book-wide members of that frame family (WEB 4:1, 4:7, 4:12, 4:15, 6:1, 6:16, 7:1, 13:19): members of this frame family do different work -- three open opposition-hearing episodes (WEB 4:1, 4:7, 6:1), two resolve an episode already opened (WEB 4:15, 6:16), WEB 4:12 is argued locally from its own text, and WEB 7:1 opens its own episode. This member, 13:19, is argued the same way, from its own clause: its apodosis continues the same 1cs subject unbroken from v15, and its protasis subject is inanimate, כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צָֽלֲלוּ֩ שַׁעֲרֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם, patterning with 7:1's own נִבְנְתָה֙ הַחוֹמָ֔ה rather than with the six members whose protases report an outside party hearing or arriving -- so here the frame escalates a reform already running rather than opening a fresh row-level unit. A pe (single-witness) keyed to 13:18 falls at the v18/v19 seam this row's rejected alternative litigates -- weak corroboration for a split there that the unbroken 1cs subject across the seam outweighs. A samekh (single-witness) keyed to 13:21 sits interior to the unit; a pe (single-witness) keyed to 13:22 falls at this unit's own closing edge -- weak, tier-3 corroboration for the boundary already established on other grounds. The unit closes on גַּם זֹאת֙ זָכְרָה לִּ֣י אֱלֹהַ֔י וְח֥וּסָה עָלַ֖י כְּרֹ֥ב חַסְדֶּֽךָ (web:Neh.13.22; WEB “Remember me for this also, my God, and spare me according to the greatness of your loving kindness”), the third zokrah-li closer.
